segments.src: > A warehouse isn't a place to park boxes — it's a machine for turning space, walking distance, and labor into delivery speed.
segments.tr: > 창고는 상자를 세워 두는 곳이 아니다. 공간, 이동 거리, 노동력을 배송 속도로 바꾸는 기계다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Say "warehouse" and most people picture shelves.
segments.tr: “창고”라고 하면 대부분 선반을 떠올린다.

segments.src: In supply chain terms, though, a warehouse is a decision stack: four choices that together determine how fast and how cheaply an order gets out the door.
segments.tr: 하지만 공급망 관점에서 창고는 의사결정의 집합이다. 네 가지 선택이 합쳐져 주문이 얼마나 빠르고 저렴하게 출고되는지를 결정한다.

segments.src: Siting — where do you put the building?**
segments.tr: 입지 선정: 건물을 어디에 둘 것인가?**

segments.src: Every location is a tug-of-war.
segments.tr: 모든 위치는 줄다리기다.

segments.src: Sit close to your customers and outbound delivery gets cheap and fast, but land and labor cost more.
segments.tr: 고객 가까이에 두면 출고 배송은 싸고 빨라지지만, 토지와 인건비가 더 든다.

segments.src: Sit close to the port or the factory and inbound freight gets cheap, but every order travels farther.
segments.tr: 항구나 공장 가까이에 두면 입고 운송비는 싸지만, 주문마다 이동 거리가 길어진다.

segments.src: Planners also weigh labor availability (can you actually hire 400 people in November?), highway and rail access, property taxes, and how many other companies are already bidding for the same workers.
segments.tr: 계획자는 노동력 확보 가능성(11월에 직원 400명을 실제로 뽑을 수 있는가?), 고속도로와 철도 접근성, 재산세, 같은 인력을 두고 경쟁하는 다른 기업이 얼마나 많은지도 함께 따진다.

segments.src: A common starting tool is the **center of gravity method**: plot demand on a map, weight each point by volume, and find the balance point.
segments.tr: 흔히 쓰는 출발점 도구는 **무게중심법**이다. 지도에 수요를 찍고 각 지점을 물량으로 가중해 균형점을 찾는다.

segments.src: It's a first draft, not an answer — the real site has to have power, a highway ramp, and people.
segments.tr: 이것은 답이 아니라 초안이다. 실제 부지에는 전력, 고속도로 진입로, 그리고 사람이 있어야 한다.

segments.src: Layout — how does product flow through it?**
segments.tr: 레이아웃: 제품은 내부에서 어떻게 흐르는가?**

segments.src: Goods generally move: receiving → putaway → storage → picking → packing → shipping.
segments.tr: 물품은 보통 이렇게 움직인다: 입고 → 적치 → 보관 → 피킹 → 포장 → 출고.

segments.src: The layout's job is to make that path short and keep flows from crossing.
segments.tr: 레이아웃의 역할은 이 경로를 짧게 만들고 흐름이 서로 교차하지 않게 하는 것이다.

segments.src: Two classic shapes:
segments.tr: 대표적인 두 가지 형태가 있다:

segments.src: - **I-flow (through-flow):** docks on opposite ends, product moves straight across. Simple, good for high-volume, cross-dock-heavy operations.
segments.tr: - **I자형 흐름(관통형):** 도크가 양 끝에 있고 제품이 곧게 가로질러 이동한다. 단순하고, 물량이 많고 크로스도킹이 많은 운영에 적합하다.

segments.src: - **U-flow:** receiving and shipping on the same wall. Fast-moving items sit near that wall so they're close to both, and one dock crew can flex between inbound and outbound.
segments.tr: - **U자형 흐름:** 입고와 출고가 같은 벽에 있다. 회전이 빠른 품목을 그 벽 근처에 두면 입고와 출고 양쪽 모두와 가까워지고, 한 도크 인원이 입고와 출고를 오가며 일할 수 있다.

segments.src: Picking — where the labor actually goes.**
segments.tr: 피킹: 노동력이 실제로 쓰이는 곳.**

segments.src: Order picking is typically the single largest labor line in a distribution center, and in manual operations, studies consistently find that *walking* eats roughly half of a picker's time.
segments.tr: 주문 피킹은 보통 물류센터에서 가장 큰 단일 인건비 항목이다. 수작업 운영을 조사한 연구들은 일관되게 *이동*이 피커 시간의 약 절반을 잡아먹는다고 보고한다.

segments.src: That's why almost every improvement idea is really a walking-reduction idea:
segments.tr: 그래서 거의 모든 개선 아이디어는 사실상 이동 거리를 줄이는 아이디어다:

segments.src: - **Slotting:** put the fast movers in the "golden zone" (waist-to-shoulder height, near the pack stations) and the slow movers up high or far back. Usually driven by **ABC analysis** — the top ~20% of SKUs often drive ~80% of the picks.
segments.tr: - **슬로팅:** 빠르게 나가는 품목은 “골든존”(허리에서 어깨 높이, 포장대 근처)에 두고, 느리게 나가는 품목은 높은 곳이나 깊숙한 곳에 둔다. 보통 **ABC 분석**으로 정하며, 상위 약 20%의 SKU가 피킹의 약 80%를 차지하는 경우가 많다.

segments.src: - **Batch picking:** grab items for 12 orders in one trip instead of walking the aisle 12 times.
segments.tr: - **배치 피킹:** 통로를 12번 걷는 대신 한 번의 이동으로 주문 12건의 품목을 한꺼번에 집는다.

segments.src: - **Zone picking:** each worker owns one area; totes move between zones by conveyor.
segments.tr: - **존 피킹:** 작업자 한 명이 구역 하나를 맡고, 토트는 컨베이어를 타고 구역 사이를 이동한다.

segments.src: - **Goods-to-person:** stop walking entirely — bring the shelf to the human.
segments.tr: - **상품-to-사람(Goods-to-person):** 걷는 것을 아예 없앤다. 선반을 사람에게 가져다준다.

segments.src: Automation — how much steel do you buy?**
segments.tr: 자동화: 설비에 얼마나 투자할 것인가?**

segments.src: The menu runs from cheap and flexible to expensive and fast: barcode scanners → pick-to-light and voice picking → conveyors and sorters → **AMRs** (mobile robots that carry totes or whole shelving pods) → **AS/RS** (automated storage and retrieval systems: cranes or shuttles in dense racking).
segments.tr: 선택지는 저렴하고 유연한 것에서 비싸고 빠른 것까지 이어진다: 바코드 스캐너 → 픽투라이트(pick-to-light)와 음성 피킹 → 컨베이어와 분류기 → **AMR**(토트나 선반 세트를 나르는 이동형 로봇) → **AS/RS**(고밀도 랙에서 크레인이나 셔틀을 쓰는 자동 보관·출고 시스템).

segments.src: The trade-off is blunt:
segments.tr: 트레이드오프는 분명하다:

segments.src: fixed automation  = high throughput, low flexibility, long payback (often 5-10 years)
segments.tr: fixed automation  = high throughput, low flexibility, long payback (often 5-10 years)

segments.src: mobile robots     = lower throughput per unit, but you can add or remove them
segments.tr: mobile robots     = lower throughput per unit, but you can add or remove them

segments.src: Fixed conveyor is poured concrete — great if your volume and product mix are stable for a decade.
segments.tr: 고정형 컨베이어는 콘크리트를 부어 만든 구조물과 같다. 물량과 품목 구성이 10년 동안 안정적이라면 훌륭하다.

segments.src: If your SKU mix changes every season, that steel becomes a cage.
segments.tr: SKU 구성이 시즌마다 바뀐다면 그 철골 구조물은 족쇄가 된다.

segments.src: And none of it works without a **WMS** (warehouse management system) telling everyone and everything where to go.
segments.tr: 그리고 이 모든 설비는 모든 사람과 모든 물품에게 어디로 가야 하는지 알려주는 **WMS**(창고관리시스템) 없이는 작동하지 않는다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상 속에서

segments.src: You order a phone case at 11 p.m.
segments.tr: 화요일 밤 11시에 휴대폰 케이스를 주문한다.

segments.src: on a Tuesday and it's on your porch Thursday morning.
segments.tr: 목요일 아침이면 케이스가 현관 앞에 도착해 있다.

segments.src: Here's what those four decisions did for you.
segments.tr: 이 네 가지 결정이 당신을 위해 무엇을 했는지 살펴보자.

segments.src: **Siting:** the item shipped from a fulfillment center outside Columbus, Ohio — one of the most crowded distribution corridors in the country, along with Indianapolis, Memphis, and California's Inland Empire.
segments.tr: **입지 선정:** 이 물건은 오하이오주 콜럼버스 외곽의 풀필먼트 센터에서 출고되었다. 그곳은 인디애나폴리스, 멤피스, 캘리포니아의 인랜드 엠파이어와 함께 미국에서 가장 붐비는 물류 회랑 중 하나다.

segments.src: Central Ohio is popular partly because a single day's truck drive from there reaches a very large share of the U.S.
segments.tr: 중부 오하이오가 인기 있는 이유 중 하나는 그곳에서 하루 트럭 운행 거리 안에 미국의

segments.src: population.
segments.tr: 인구 상당수가 닿기 때문이다.

segments.src: The company paid for that: industrial space is quoted in dollars per square foot per year, and rents run from the high single digits in parts of the Midwest to well into the teens and above in Southern California.
segments.tr: 그 비용은 회사가 냈다. 산업용 공간은 제곱피트당 연간 달러로 견적되며, 임대료는 중서부 일부 지역의 한 자릿수 후반에서 남부 캘리포니아의 10달러 중반 이상까지 이어진다.

segments.src: That premium buys a delivery promise.
segments.tr: 그 프리미엄이 배송 약속을 산다.

segments.src: **Layout and slotting:** your case wasn't stored next to other phone cases.
segments.tr: **레이아웃과 슬로팅:** 당신의 케이스는 다른 휴대폰 케이스 옆에 보관되지 않았다.

segments.src: Many large fulfillment centers use *random* (sometimes called chaotic) storage — items go wherever there's an open bin, and the WMS remembers.
segments.tr: 많은 대형 풀필먼트 센터는 *랜덤*(때로는 카오스라고도 부른다) 보관 방식을 쓴다. 물품은 비어 있는 빈(bin)이 있는 곳이면 어디든 들어가고, WMS가 위치를 기억한다.

segments.src: It sounds like chaos; it's actually better cube utilization and shorter walks, because popular items end up scattered near many pick paths instead of clustered in one aisle everyone has to visit.
segments.tr: 혼란스러워 보이지만 실제로는 공간 활용도가 높고 이동 거리가 짧다. 인기 품목이 모두 한 통로에 몰리지 않고 여러 피킹 경로 근처에 흩어져 있기 때문이다.

segments.src: **Picking:** a worker pushing a cart of totes picked your case as part of a batch of 20-some orders, guided by a handheld that sequenced the route.
segments.tr: **피킹:** 토트를 실은 카트를 밀던 작업자가, 경로를 순서대로 안내하는 핸디 단말기의 지시에 따라 20여 건의 주문으로 묶인 배치의 일부로 당신의 케이스를 집었다.

segments.src: Or a robot drove a whole shelving pod to a stationary picker who never took a step.
segments.tr: 아니면 로봇이 선반 한 세트를 통째로 가져와, 한 걸음도 움직이지 않은 작업자에게 전달했을 수도 있다.

segments.src: **Automation:** at pack-out, your box hit a conveyor, got weighed (a weight mismatch flags a wrong-item pick), passed a scanner, and a sorter diverted it down the chute for the right carrier trailer.
segments.tr: **자동화:** 포장 출고 단계에서 상자는 컨베이어에 올라 무게를 측정받았다(무게 불일치는 잘못 집힌 품목을 표시한다). 스캐너를 지난 뒤 분류기가 올바른 운송사 트레일러로 이어지는 슈트 쪽으로 보냈다.

segments.src: That trailer left on a scheduled cutoff — miss the cutoff and "Thursday" becomes "Friday."
segments.tr: 그 트레일러는 정해진 마감 시간에 떠났다. 마감을 놓치면 “목요일”은 “금요일”이 된다.

segments.src: Which is the real lesson: the delivery date you saw at checkout was mostly decided by a building's floor plan and a truck's departure time.
segments.tr: 이것이 진짜 교훈이다. 결제 화면에서 본 배송일은 대부분 건물의 평면도와 트럭의 출발 시각이 정한 것이다.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 세 줄 요약

segments.src: 1. Warehouse siting trades outbound speed and cost against land, labor, and inbound freight — you can't optimize all of them.
segments.tr: 1. 창고 입지는 출고 속도와 비용을 토지, 노동력, 입고 운송비와 맞바꾼다. 이 모두를 동시에 최적화할 수는 없다.

segments.src: 2. Layout and slotting exist to kill walking, because walking is roughly half of picking time and picking is the biggest labor cost.
segments.tr: 2. 레이아웃과 슬로팅은 이동을 없애기 위해 존재한다. 이동은 피킹 시간의 약 절반이고, 피킹은 가장 큰 인건비이기 때문이다.

segments.src: 3. Automation buys throughput with capital and gives up flexibility — the right level depends on how stable your volume and product mix are.
segments.tr: 3. 자동화는 자본을 들여 처리량을 사고 유연성을 내준다. 적정 수준은 물량과 품목 구성이 얼마나 안정적인지에 달려 있다.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 자가 점검 퀴즈

segments.src: **1.** In a typical manual, picker-to-goods operation, the largest single chunk of a picker's time goes to:
segments.tr: **1.** 일반적인 수작업 피커-물품 방식의 운영에서 피커 시간의 가장 큰 몫은 어디에 쓰이는가?

segments.src: A) scanning barcodes
segments.tr: A) 바코드 스캔

segments.src: B) traveling (walking) between locations
segments.tr: B) 위치 사이 이동(걷기)

segments.src: C) packing cartons
segments.tr: C) 상자 포장

segments.src: D) waiting for a forklift
segments.tr: D) 지게차를 기다리기

segments.src: **2.** (O/X) Placing your fastest-moving SKUs at waist height near the pack stations is called *slotting*, and its main purpose is to reduce travel time.
segments.tr: **2.** (O/X) 가장 빨리 나가는 SKU를 허리 높이로 포장대 근처에 두는 것을 *슬로팅*이라 하며, 주된 목적은 이동 시간을 줄이는 것이다.

segments.src: **3.** A retailer's volume triples every Q4 and its product mix changes every season.
segments.tr: **3.** 한 소매업체의 물량은 매 4분기마다 세 배로 늘고, 품목 구성은 시즌마다 바뀐다.

segments.src: Which automation choice generally fits better?
segments.tr: 어떤 자동화 선택이 일반적으로 더 잘 맞는가?

segments.src: A) A fixed conveyor-and-sortation system sized for peak
segments.tr: A) 피크 물량에 맞춰 설계한 고정형 컨베이어·분류 시스템

segments.src: B) Mobile robots (AMRs) that can be added or removed as volume changes
segments.tr: B) 물량 변화에 따라 추가하거나 뺄 수 있는 이동형 로봇(AMR)

segments.src: C) A full AS/RS crane system
segments.tr: C) 완전한 AS/RS 크레인 시스템

segments.src: D) No technology at all
segments.tr: D) 어떤 기술도 쓰지 않음

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Slotting** — deciding which item goes in which storage location, usually to minimize picker travel.
segments.tr: - **슬로팅**: 어떤 품목을 어느 보관 위치에 둘지 정하는 것. 보통 피커의 이동 거리를 최소화하기 위해서다.

segments.src: - **ABC analysis** — ranking SKUs by activity (A = fastest moving) so storage and effort go where the volume is.
segments.tr: - **ABC 분석**: SKU를 활동량 기준으로 순위 매기는 것(A = 가장 빠르게 나가는 품목). 보관과 노력을 물량이 많은 곳에 집중하기 위해서다.

segments.src: - **Batch picking** — picking items for multiple orders in a single trip through the warehouse, then sorting them by order afterward.
segments.tr: - **배치 피킹**: 창고를 한 번 지나가며 여러 주문의 품목을 한꺼번에 집은 뒤, 나중에 주문별로 분류하는 것.

segments.src: - **Goods-to-person (G2P)** — automation that brings inventory to a stationary worker instead of sending the worker to the inventory.
segments.tr: - **상품-to-사람(G2P)**: 작업자를 재고 쪽으로 보내는 대신, 재고를 제자리에 있는 작업자에게 가져다주는 자동화.

segments.src: - **Cross-docking** — moving freight straight from an inbound trailer to an outbound one with little or no storage in between.
segments.tr: - **크로스도킹**: 중간 보관을 거의 하지 않고, 입고 트레일러의 화물을 곧바로 출고 트레일러로 옮기는 것.

segments.src: *Answers: **1) B** — travel typically accounts for around half of order-picking time in manual operations, which is why layout and slotting matter so much.
segments.tr: *정답: **1) B**. 수작업 운영에서 이동은 보통 피킹 시간의 절반 가량을 차지하며, 그래서 레이아웃과 슬로팅이 중요하다.

segments.src: **2) O (True)** — slotting fast movers into the golden zone near pack-out shortens both walking and reaching.
segments.tr: **2) O (참)**. 골든존의 포장대 근처에 빠른 품목을 슬로팅하면 걷기와 손 뻗기가 모두 줄어든다.

segments.src: **3) B** — AMRs scale incrementally and tolerate a changing SKU mix; fixed conveyor and AS/RS deliver higher throughput but lock in a layout and need stable, predictable volume to justify the payback period.*
segments.tr: **3) B**. AMR은 점진적으로 확장할 수 있고 변화하는 SKU 구성도 감당한다. 고정형 컨베이어와 AS/RS는 처리량이 더 높지만 레이아웃을 고정하고, 투자회수기간을 정당화하려면 안정적이고 예측 가능한 물량이 필요하다.*

zh.title: [物流 101 #7] 决定你的订单明天能否送达的那座建筑

segments.src: > A warehouse isn't a place to park boxes — it's a machine for turning space, walking distance, and labor into delivery speed.
segments.tr: > 仓库不是堆放箱子的地方——它是一台把空间、步行距离和人力转化为配送速度的机器。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日概念

segments.src: Say "warehouse" and most people picture shelves.
segments.tr: 提到“仓库”，大多数人想到的是货架。

segments.src: In supply chain terms, though, a warehouse is a decision stack: four choices that together determine how fast and how cheaply an order gets out the door.
segments.tr: 但从供应链的角度看，仓库是一组决策堆栈：四项选择共同决定了订单能以多快的速度、多低的成本发出。

segments.src: Siting — where do you put the building?**
segments.tr: 选址——把仓库建在哪里？**

segments.src: Every location is a tug-of-war.
segments.tr: 每个选址都是一场拉锯战。

segments.src: Sit close to your customers and outbound delivery gets cheap and fast, but land and labor cost more.
segments.tr: 靠近客户，出库配送既便宜又快，但土地和人力成本更高。

segments.src: Sit close to the port or the factory and inbound freight gets cheap, but every order travels farther.
segments.tr: 靠近港口或工厂，入库运费便宜，但每张订单的运输距离更远。

segments.src: Planners also weigh labor availability (can you actually hire 400 people in November?), highway and rail access, property taxes, and how many other companies are already bidding for the same workers.
segments.tr: 规划者还要权衡劳动力供给（11 月能否招到 400 名员工？）、公路和铁路交通、房产税，以及有多少其他企业正在争夺同一批工人。

segments.src: A common starting tool is the **center of gravity method**: plot demand on a map, weight each point by volume, and find the balance point.
segments.tr: 常用的起步工具是**重心法**：在地图上标出需求点，按体量为每个点加权，再找出平衡点。

segments.src: It's a first draft, not an answer — the real site has to have power, a highway ramp, and people.
segments.tr: 这只是初稿而非结论——真正的选址还必须具备电力、高速公路匝道和人力。

segments.src: Layout — how does product flow through it?**
segments.tr: 布局——商品如何在其中流动？**

segments.src: Goods generally move: receiving → putaway → storage → picking → packing → shipping.
segments.tr: 货物通常按以下顺序移动：收货 → 上架 → 存储 → 拣选 → 打包 → 发运。

segments.src: The layout's job is to make that path short and keep flows from crossing.
segments.tr: 布局的目标是让这条路径尽可能短，并避免物流路线交叉。

segments.src: Two classic shapes:
segments.tr: 两种经典形态：

segments.src: - **I-flow (through-flow):** docks on opposite ends, product moves straight across. Simple, good for high-volume, cross-dock-heavy operations.
segments.tr: - **I 型流（直通型）：** 月台位于两端，商品笔直穿过。结构简单，适合大批量、以越库为主的作业。

segments.src: - **U-flow:** receiving and shipping on the same wall. Fast-moving items sit near that wall so they're close to both, and one dock crew can flex between inbound and outbound.
segments.tr: - **U 型流：** 收货和发货位于同一面墙。快速周转的商品放在这面墙附近，离收发两端都近，并且同一组月台人员可以在入库和出库之间灵活调配。

segments.src: Picking — where the labor actually goes.**
segments.tr: 拣选——人力真正消耗在哪里。**

segments.src: Order picking is typically the single largest labor line in a distribution center, and in manual operations, studies consistently find that *walking* eats roughly half of a picker's time.
segments.tr: 订单拣选通常是配送中心中单项最大的人力成本，而在人工作业中，研究一致发现，*步行*大约占拣货员时间的一半。

segments.src: That's why almost every improvement idea is really a walking-reduction idea:
segments.tr: 这就是为什么几乎所有改进思路本质上都是减少步行：

segments.src: - **Slotting:** put the fast movers in the "golden zone" (waist-to-shoulder height, near the pack stations) and the slow movers up high or far back. Usually driven by **ABC analysis** — the top ~20% of SKUs often drive ~80% of the picks.
segments.tr: - **货位优化：** 把快速周转的商品放在“黄金区”（腰部到肩部高度，靠近打包台），慢速周转的商品放在高处或仓库深处。通常依据 **ABC 分析**进行——前约 20% 的 SKU 往往贡献约 80% 的拣选量。

segments.src: - **Batch picking:** grab items for 12 orders in one trip instead of walking the aisle 12 times.
segments.tr: - **批量拣选：** 一次行程为 12 张订单同时拣货，而不是走 12 趟货架通道。

segments.src: - **Zone picking:** each worker owns one area; totes move between zones by conveyor.
segments.tr: - **分区拣选：** 每位员工负责一个区域，周转箱通过输送线在各区域之间流转。

segments.src: - **Goods-to-person:** stop walking entirely — bring the shelf to the human.
segments.tr: - **货到人：** 彻底不用步行——把货架送到人面前。

segments.src: Automation — how much steel do you buy?**
segments.tr: 自动化——该投入多少钢材？**

segments.src: The menu runs from cheap and flexible to expensive and fast: barcode scanners → pick-to-light and voice picking → conveyors and sorters → **AMRs** (mobile robots that carry totes or whole shelving pods) → **AS/RS** (automated storage and retrieval systems: cranes or shuttles in dense racking).
segments.tr: 选项从低成本、高灵活性到高成本、高速度依次排列：条码扫描器 → 电子标签拣选和语音拣选 → 输送线和分拣机 → **AMR**（搬运周转箱或整组货架的移动机器人）→ **AS/RS**（自动化立体仓库系统：在高密度货架中使用堆垛机或穿梭车）。

segments.src: The trade-off is blunt:
segments.tr: 取舍很直接：

segments.src: fixed automation  = high throughput, low flexibility, long payback (often 5-10 years)
segments.tr: fixed automation  = high throughput, low flexibility, long payback (often 5-10 years)

segments.src: mobile robots     = lower throughput per unit, but you can add or remove them
segments.tr: mobile robots     = lower throughput per unit, but you can add or remove them

segments.src: Fixed conveyor is poured concrete — great if your volume and product mix are stable for a decade.
segments.tr: 固定式输送线就像浇筑的混凝土——如果你的业务量和产品组合十年内都稳定，它非常理想。

segments.src: If your SKU mix changes every season, that steel becomes a cage.
segments.tr: 如果你的 SKU 组合每季都在变化，这些钢材就会成为牢笼。

segments.src: And none of it works without a **WMS** (warehouse management system) telling everyone and everything where to go.
segments.tr: 而且没有 **WMS**（仓储管理系统）告诉所有人和所有设备该去哪里，这一切都无法运转。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活中的体现

segments.src: You order a phone case at 11 p.m.
segments.tr: 你在周二晚上 11 点下单了一个手机壳，

segments.src: on a Tuesday and it's on your porch Thursday morning.
segments.tr: 周四早上它就出现在你家门口。

segments.src: Here's what those four decisions did for you.
segments.tr: 这四项决策分别为你做了什么。

segments.src: **Siting:** the item shipped from a fulfillment center outside Columbus, Ohio — one of the most crowded distribution corridors in the country, along with Indianapolis, Memphis, and California's Inland Empire.
segments.tr: **选址：** 这件商品从俄亥俄州哥伦布市郊的配送中心发出——这是全美最拥挤的配送走廊之一，与印第安纳波利斯、孟菲斯以及加州的内陆帝国区并列。

segments.src: Central Ohio is popular partly because a single day's truck drive from there reaches a very large share of the U.S.
segments.tr: 中俄亥俄州受欢迎，部分原因是从那里出发，一天的卡车车程就能覆盖美国很大比例的

segments.src: population.
segments.tr: 人口。

segments.src: The company paid for that: industrial space is quoted in dollars per square foot per year, and rents run from the high single digits in parts of the Midwest to well into the teens and above in Southern California.
segments.tr: 这笔费用由企业承担：工业用地的报价以每平方英尺每年多少美元计，中西部部分地区的租金在个位数高段，而南加州则达到十几美元甚至更高。

segments.src: That premium buys a delivery promise.
segments.tr: 这笔溢价买到的是配送时效承诺。

segments.src: **Layout and slotting:** your case wasn't stored next to other phone cases.
segments.tr: **布局与货位：** 你的手机壳并没有被存放在其他手机壳旁边。

segments.src: Many large fulfillment centers use *random* (sometimes called chaotic) storage — items go wherever there's an open bin, and the WMS remembers.
segments.tr: 许多大型配送中心采用*随机*（有时称为混乱）存储——商品放进任何空闲货位，由 WMS 记录位置。

segments.src: It sounds like chaos; it's actually better cube utilization and shorter walks, because popular items end up scattered near many pick paths instead of clustered in one aisle everyone has to visit.
segments.tr: 这听起来很混乱，实际上却能提高空间利用率、缩短步行距离，因为热门商品分散在众多拣选路径附近，而不是集中在一条所有人都必须经过的通道里。

segments.src: **Picking:** a worker pushing a cart of totes picked your case as part of a batch of 20-some orders, guided by a handheld that sequenced the route.
segments.tr: **拣选：** 一名推着周转箱车的员工，把你的手机壳放进一批二十多张订单的拣选任务中，由手持终端规划路线。

segments.src: Or a robot drove a whole shelving pod to a stationary picker who never took a step.
segments.tr: 或者，一台机器人把整组货架运到一位从不需要迈步的固定拣货员面前。

segments.src: **Automation:** at pack-out, your box hit a conveyor, got weighed (a weight mismatch flags a wrong-item pick), passed a scanner, and a sorter diverted it down the chute for the right carrier trailer.
segments.tr: **自动化：** 在出库打包环节，你的包裹经过输送线，被称重（重量不符会标记拣错商品）、经过扫描，然后被分拣机导入通往正确承运车辆的滑道。

segments.src: That trailer left on a scheduled cutoff — miss the cutoff and "Thursday" becomes "Friday."
segments.tr: 该车辆按计划的截止时间发车——错过截止时间，“周四”就会变成“周五”。

segments.src: Which is the real lesson: the delivery date you saw at checkout was mostly decided by a building's floor plan and a truck's departure time.
segments.tr: 这才是真正的启示：你在结账时看到的送达日期，很大程度上是由建筑的平面布局和卡车的发车时间决定的。

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 三行总结

segments.src: 1. Warehouse siting trades outbound speed and cost against land, labor, and inbound freight — you can't optimize all of them.
segments.tr: 1. 仓库选址是在出库速度与成本、土地、人力和入库运费之间的权衡——你无法同时优化所有这些因素。

segments.src: 2. Layout and slotting exist to kill walking, because walking is roughly half of picking time and picking is the biggest labor cost.
segments.tr: 2. 布局和货位规划的目的是减少步行，因为步行约占拣选时间的一半，而拣选是最大的人力成本。

segments.src: 3. Automation buys throughput with capital and gives up flexibility — the right level depends on how stable your volume and product mix are.
segments.tr: 3. 自动化以资本换取吞吐量，同时牺牲灵活性——合适的自动化水平取决于你的业务量和产品组合有多稳定。

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 自测题

segments.src: **1.** In a typical manual, picker-to-goods operation, the largest single chunk of a picker's time goes to:
segments.tr: **1.** 在典型的人工“拣货员到货物”作业中，拣货员时间中占比最大的部分用于：

segments.src: A) scanning barcodes
segments.tr: A) 扫描条码

segments.src: B) traveling (walking) between locations
segments.tr: B) 在各库位之间行走（步行）

segments.src: C) packing cartons
segments.tr: C) 打包纸箱

segments.src: D) waiting for a forklift
segments.tr: D) 等待叉车

segments.src: **2.** (O/X) Placing your fastest-moving SKUs at waist height near the pack stations is called *slotting*, and its main purpose is to reduce travel time.
segments.tr: **2.** （O/X）将周转最快的 SKU 放在腰部高度、靠近打包台的位置，称为*货位优化*，其主要目的是减少行走时间。

segments.src: **3.** A retailer's volume triples every Q4 and its product mix changes every season.
segments.tr: **3.** 某零售商的业务量每到第四季度增至三倍，且产品组合每季都会变化。

segments.src: Which automation choice generally fits better?
segments.tr: 以下哪种自动化方案通常更适合？

segments.src: A) A fixed conveyor-and-sortation system sized for peak
segments.tr: A) 按高峰负荷配置的固定式输送与分拣系统

segments.src: B) Mobile robots (AMRs) that can be added or removed as volume changes
segments.tr: B) 可随业务量增减而增减的移动机器人（AMR）

segments.src: C) A full AS/RS crane system
segments.tr: C) 完整的 AS/RS 堆垛机系统

segments.src: D) No technology at all
segments.tr: D) 完全不使用任何技术

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日术语

segments.src: - **Slotting** — deciding which item goes in which storage location, usually to minimize picker travel.
segments.tr: - **货位优化（Slotting）**——决定每件商品存放在哪个存储位置，通常以减少拣货员行走距离为目标。

segments.src: - **ABC analysis** — ranking SKUs by activity (A = fastest moving) so storage and effort go where the volume is.
segments.tr: - **ABC 分析**——按照出入库活跃度对 SKU 排序（A 类 = 周转最快），使存储空间和人力投入集中在业务量最大的地方。

segments.src: - **Batch picking** — picking items for multiple orders in a single trip through the warehouse, then sorting them by order afterward.
segments.tr: - **批量拣选**——在一次穿越仓库的行程中为多张订单拣货，之后再按订单分拣。

segments.src: - **Goods-to-person (G2P)** — automation that brings inventory to a stationary worker instead of sending the worker to the inventory.
segments.tr: - **货到人（G2P）**——让库存送到固定不动的工作人员面前，而不是让工作人员去找库存的自动化方式。

segments.src: - **Cross-docking** — moving freight straight from an inbound trailer to an outbound one with little or no storage in between.
segments.tr: - **越库（Cross-docking）**——将货物从入库车辆直接转运到出库车辆，中间很少或不做存储。

segments.src: *Answers: **1) B** — travel typically accounts for around half of order-picking time in manual operations, which is why layout and slotting matter so much.
segments.tr: *答案：**1) B** ——在人工拣选作业中，行走通常占订单拣选时间的一半左右，这就是布局和货位规划如此重要的原因。

segments.src: **2) O (True)** — slotting fast movers into the golden zone near pack-out shortens both walking and reaching.
segments.tr: **2) O（正确）** ——将快速周转的商品放在黄金区附近，可同时缩短行走和取放距离。

segments.src: **3) B** — AMRs scale incrementally and tolerate a changing SKU mix; fixed conveyor and AS/RS deliver higher throughput but lock in a layout and need stable, predictable volume to justify the payback period.*
segments.tr: **3) B** ——AMR 可以逐步扩展，并能适应变化的 SKU 组合；固定输送线和 AS/RS 虽然吞吐量更高，但会锁定布局，并且需要稳定、可预测的业务量才能证明投资回收期合理。*

hi.title: [Logistics 101 #7] वह इमारत जो तय करती है कि आपका ऑर्डर कल पहुंचेगा या नहीं

segments.src: > A warehouse isn't a place to park boxes — it's a machine for turning space, walking distance, and labor into delivery speed.
segments.tr: > गोदाम सामान रखने की जगह नहीं है — यह जगह, पैदल दूरी और श्रम को डिलीवरी की रफ़्तार में बदलने वाली एक मशीन है।

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## आज की अवधारणा

segments.src: Say "warehouse" and most people picture shelves.
segments.tr: ज़्यादातर लोग "गोदाम" सुनते ही अलमारियों (शेल्फ़) की कल्पना करते हैं।

segments.src: In supply chain terms, though, a warehouse is a decision stack: four choices that together determine how fast and how cheaply an order gets out the door.
segments.tr: लेकिन आपूर्ति श्रृंखला (supply chain) की भाषा में, गोदाम एक निर्णय-स्तंभ है: चार विकल्पों का समूह, जो मिलकर तय करते हैं कि कोई ऑर्डर कितनी तेज़ी से और कितनी कम लागत पर बाहर निकलेगा।

segments.src: Siting — where do you put the building?**
segments.tr: स्थान-चयन — इमारत कहाँ बनाएँ?**

segments.src: Every location is a tug-of-war.
segments.tr: हर स्थान एक खींचतान है।

segments.src: Sit close to your customers and outbound delivery gets cheap and fast, but land and labor cost more.
segments.tr: अपने ग्राहकों के पास होने पर बाहरी डिलीवरी सस्ती और तेज़ होती है, पर ज़मीन और श्रम महँगे पड़ते हैं।

segments.src: Sit close to the port or the factory and inbound freight gets cheap, but every order travels farther.
segments.tr: बंदरगाह या फ़ैक्ट्री के पास होने पर आने वाला माल (inbound freight) सस्ता पड़ता है, पर हर ऑर्डर को ज़्यादा दूरी तय करनी पड़ती है।

segments.src: Planners also weigh labor availability (can you actually hire 400 people in November?), highway and rail access, property taxes, and how many other companies are already bidding for the same workers.
segments.tr: योजनाकार श्रम की उपलब्धता (क्या नवंबर में सचमुच 400 लोगों को काम पर रखा जा सकता है?), हाईवे और रेल की पहुँच, संपत्ति कर, और उसी श्रम के लिए कितनी और कंपनियाँ बोली लगा रही हैं, इन सब को भी तौलते हैं।

segments.src: A common starting tool is the **center of gravity method**: plot demand on a map, weight each point by volume, and find the balance point.
segments.tr: एक आम शुरुआती उपकरण है **गुरुत्व-केंद्र विधि (center of gravity method)**: नक्शे पर माँग को चिह्नित करें, हर बिंदु को उसकी मात्रा से भार दें, और संतुलन बिंदु खोजें।

segments.src: It's a first draft, not an answer — the real site has to have power, a highway ramp, and people.
segments.tr: यह एक प्रारंभिक मसौदा है, अंतिम उत्तर नहीं — असली स्थल पर बिजली, हाईवे का ramp और लोग भी होने चाहिए।

segments.src: Layout — how does product flow through it?**
segments.tr: लेआउट — उत्पाद इसमें से कैसे बहता है?**

segments.src: Goods generally move: receiving → putaway → storage → picking → packing → shipping.
segments.tr: सामान आम तौर पर इस क्रम में चलता है: प्राप्ति (receiving) → भंडारण में रखना (putaway) → संग्रहण (storage) → चुनना (picking) → पैकिंग → शिपिंग।

segments.src: The layout's job is to make that path short and keep flows from crossing.
segments.tr: लेआउट का काम है इस रास्ते को छोटा रखना और प्रवाह को एक-दूसरे को काटने से बचाना।

segments.src: Two classic shapes:
segments.tr: दो क्लासिक आकार:

segments.src: - **I-flow (through-flow):** docks on opposite ends, product moves straight across. Simple, good for high-volume, cross-dock-heavy operations.
segments.tr: - **I-प्रवाह (through-flow):** दोनों छोर पर डॉक, माल सीधे एक तरफ़ से दूसरी तरफ़ जाता है। सरल है, उच्च मात्रा और cross-dock-प्रधान संचालन के लिए अच्छा।

segments.src: - **U-flow:** receiving and shipping on the same wall. Fast-moving items sit near that wall so they're close to both, and one dock crew can flex between inbound and outbound.
segments.tr: - **U-प्रवाह:** प्राप्ति और शिपिंग एक ही दीवार पर। तेज़ी से बिकने वाली चीज़ें उसी दीवार के पास रखी जाती हैं ताकि दोनों के करीब रहें, और एक ही डॉक-दल आने और जाने वाले माल के बीच लचीले ढंग से काम कर सके।

segments.src: Picking — where the labor actually goes.**
segments.tr: चुनना (picking) — श्रम वास्तव में कहाँ जाता है।**

segments.src: Order picking is typically the single largest labor line in a distribution center, and in manual operations, studies consistently find that *walking* eats roughly half of a picker's time.
segments.tr: ऑर्डर-पिकिंग आम तौर पर वितरण केंद्र (distribution center) की सबसे बड़ी अकेली श्रम-लागत होती है, और मैनुअल संचालन में अध्ययन लगातार बताते हैं कि चुनने वाले के समय का लगभग आधा हिस्सा *चलने* में जाता है।

segments.src: That's why almost every improvement idea is really a walking-reduction idea:
segments.tr: इसीलिए लगभग हर सुधार का विचार असल में पैदल-चाल घटाने का विचार होता है:

segments.src: - **Slotting:** put the fast movers in the "golden zone" (waist-to-shoulder height, near the pack stations) and the slow movers up high or far back. Usually driven by **ABC analysis** — the top ~20% of SKUs often drive ~80% of the picks.
segments.tr: - **स्लॉटिंग:** तेज़ी से चलने वाले सामान को "गोल्डन ज़ोन" (कमर से कंधे तक की ऊँचाई, पैकिंग स्टेशन के पास) में रखें, और धीमे चलने वाले सामान को ऊपर या दूर पीछे। आम तौर पर यह **ABC विश्लेषण** से तय होता है — शीर्ष लगभग 20% SKU अक्सर लगभग 80% पिक्स करवाते हैं।

segments.src: - **Batch picking:** grab items for 12 orders in one trip instead of walking the aisle 12 times.
segments.tr: - **बैच पिकिंग:** 12 ऑर्डरों का सामान एक ही चक्कर में उठाना, बजाय इसके कि गलियारे में 12 बार चला जाए।

segments.src: - **Zone picking:** each worker owns one area; totes move between zones by conveyor.
segments.tr: - **ज़ोन पिकिंग:** हर कर्मचारी का एक क्षेत्र होता है; टोट्स (ट्रे/डिब्बे) कन्वेयर से ज़ोन के बीच जाते हैं।

segments.src: - **Goods-to-person:** stop walking entirely — bring the shelf to the human.
segments.tr: - **Goods-to-person:** पैदल चलना पूरी तरह बंद — शेल्फ़ को इंसान के पास ले आएँ।

segments.src: Automation — how much steel do you buy?**
segments.tr: स्वचालन (Automation) — कितना स्टील (मशीनरी) खरीदें?**

segments.src: The menu runs from cheap and flexible to expensive and fast: barcode scanners → pick-to-light and voice picking → conveyors and sorters → **AMRs** (mobile robots that carry totes or whole shelving pods) → **AS/RS** (automated storage and retrieval systems: cranes or shuttles in dense racking).
segments.tr: विकल्पों की सूची सस्ते और लचीले से लेकर महँगे और तेज़ तक जाती है: बारकोड स्कैनर → pick-to-light और voice picking → कन्वेयर और सॉर्टर → **AMRs** (मोबाइल रोबोट जो टोट्स या पूरे शेल्फ़ पॉड उठाते हैं) → **AS/RS** (स्वचालित भंडारण और पुनर्प्राप्ति प्रणाली: घने रैक में क्रेन या शटल)।

segments.src: The trade-off is blunt:
segments.tr: व्यापार-बंद (trade-off) सीधा है:

segments.src: fixed automation  = high throughput, low flexibility, long payback (often 5-10 years)
segments.tr: fixed automation  = high throughput, low flexibility, long payback (often 5-10 years)

segments.src: mobile robots     = lower throughput per unit, but you can add or remove them
segments.tr: mobile robots     = lower throughput per unit, but you can add or remove them

segments.src: Fixed conveyor is poured concrete — great if your volume and product mix are stable for a decade.
segments.tr: स्थिर कन्वेयर पक्के कंक्रीट जैसा है — अगर आपकी मात्रा और उत्पाद-मिश्रण एक दशक तक स्थिर है तो बढ़िया।

segments.src: If your SKU mix changes every season, that steel becomes a cage.
segments.tr: अगर आपका SKU-मिश्रण हर मौसम में बदलता है, तो वही स्टील एक पिंजरा बन जाता है।

segments.src: And none of it works without a **WMS** (warehouse management system) telling everyone and everything where to go.
segments.tr: और इनमें से कुछ भी **WMS** (वेयरहाउस मैनेजमेंट सिस्टम) के बिना नहीं चलता, जो हर व्यक्ति और हर चीज़ को बताता है कि उसे कहाँ जाना है।

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## रोज़मर्रा की ज़िंदगी में

segments.src: You order a phone case at 11 p.m.
segments.tr: आप मंगलवार रात 11 बजे फ़ोन का कवर ऑर्डर करते हैं

segments.src: on a Tuesday and it's on your porch Thursday morning.
segments.tr: और वह गुरुवार सुबह आपके दरवाज़े पर होता है।

segments.src: Here's what those four decisions did for you.
segments.tr: देखिए इन चार निर्णयों ने आपके लिए क्या किया।

segments.src: **Siting:** the item shipped from a fulfillment center outside Columbus, Ohio — one of the most crowded distribution corridors in the country, along with Indianapolis, Memphis, and California's Inland Empire.
segments.tr: **स्थान-चयन:** सामान ओहायो के कोलंबस के बाहर एक फ़ुलफ़िलमेंट सेंटर से भेजा गया — देश के सबसे भीड़-भाड़ वाले वितरण गलियारों में से एक, इंडियानापोलिस, मेम्फ़िस और कैलिफ़ोर्निया के Inland Empire के साथ।

segments.src: Central Ohio is popular partly because a single day's truck drive from there reaches a very large share of the U.S.
segments.tr: मध्य ओहायो इसलिए लोकप्रिय है क्योंकि वहाँ से एक दिन की ट्रक ड्राइव में अमेरिका की एक बहुत बड़ी हिस्सेदारी

segments.src: population.
segments.tr: आबादी तक पहुँचा जा सकता है।

segments.src: The company paid for that: industrial space is quoted in dollars per square foot per year, and rents run from the high single digits in parts of the Midwest to well into the teens and above in Southern California.
segments.tr: कंपनी ने इसकी कीमत चुकाई: औद्योगिक जगह का किराया प्रति वर्ग फ़ुट प्रति वर्ष डॉलर में बताया जाता है, और मिडवेस्ट के कुछ हिस्सों में यह एकल अंकों की ऊँचाई से लेकर दक्षिणी कैलिफ़ोर्निया में दहाई से भी ऊपर तक जाता है।

segments.src: That premium buys a delivery promise.
segments.tr: वह प्रीमियम एक डिलीवरी का वादा खरीदता है।

segments.src: **Layout and slotting:** your case wasn't stored next to other phone cases.
segments.tr: **लेआउट और स्लॉटिंग:** आपका केस दूसरे फ़ोन केसों के बगल में नहीं रखा गया था।

segments.src: Many large fulfillment centers use *random* (sometimes called chaotic) storage — items go wherever there's an open bin, and the WMS remembers.
segments.tr: कई बड़े फ़ुलफ़िलमेंट सेंटर *रैंडम* (जिसे कभी-कभी केऑटिक भी कहते हैं) भंडारण का उपयोग करते हैं — सामान वहीं जाता है जहाँ कोई खाली बिन हो, और WMS याद रखता है।

segments.src: It sounds like chaos; it's actually better cube utilization and shorter walks, because popular items end up scattered near many pick paths instead of clustered in one aisle everyone has to visit.
segments.tr: यह अराजकता लगती है; असल में यह बेहतर क्यूब उपयोग और छोटी पैदल-चाल है, क्योंकि लोकप्रिय सामान कई पिक-पाथ के पास बिखरा रहता है, बजाय इसके कि एक ही गलियारे में जमा हो जिस तक सबको जाना पड़े।

segments.src: **Picking:** a worker pushing a cart of totes picked your case as part of a batch of 20-some orders, guided by a handheld that sequenced the route.
segments.tr: **पिकिंग:** टोट्स से भरी ट्रॉली धकेलते एक कर्मचारी ने 20-कुछ ऑर्डरों के बैच के हिस्से के रूप में आपका केस उठाया, और एक हैंडहेल्ड डिवाइस रास्ते को क्रम देकर मार्गदर्शन कर रहा था।

segments.src: Or a robot drove a whole shelving pod to a stationary picker who never took a step.
segments.tr: या फिर एक रोबोट पूरा शेल्फ़ पॉड उस स्थिर कर्मचारी तक ले गया जिसने एक कदम भी नहीं चला।

segments.src: **Automation:** at pack-out, your box hit a conveyor, got weighed (a weight mismatch flags a wrong-item pick), passed a scanner, and a sorter diverted it down the chute for the right carrier trailer.
segments.tr: **स्वचालन:** पैक-आउट पर आपका बॉक्स एक कन्वेयर पर पहुँचा, उसका वज़न लिया गया (वज़न का मेल न खाना गलत-आइटम पिक का संकेत है), एक स्कैनर से गुज़रा, और एक सॉर्टर ने उसे सही कैरियर ट्रेलर के लिए चूट में भेज दिया।

segments.src: That trailer left on a scheduled cutoff — miss the cutoff and "Thursday" becomes "Friday."
segments.tr: वह ट्रेलर एक तय कटऑफ़ पर निकला — कटऑफ़ चूक गए तो "गुरुवार" "शुक्रवार" बन जाता है।

segments.src: Which is the real lesson: the delivery date you saw at checkout was mostly decided by a building's floor plan and a truck's departure time.
segments.tr: और असली सबक यही है: चेकआउट पर जो डिलीवरी तारीख आपने देखी, वह ज़्यादातर एक इमारत के फ़्लोर-प्लान और एक ट्रक के प्रस्थान समय से तय हुई थी।

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## तीन-पंक्ति सार

segments.src: 1. Warehouse siting trades outbound speed and cost against land, labor, and inbound freight — you can't optimize all of them.
segments.tr: 1. गोदाम का स्थान-चयन बाहरी गति और लागत को ज़मीन, श्रम और आने वाले माल के मुक़ाबले तौलता है — आप इन सबको एक साथ अनुकूलित नहीं कर सकते।

segments.src: 2. Layout and slotting exist to kill walking, because walking is roughly half of picking time and picking is the biggest labor cost.
segments.tr: 2. लेआउट और स्लॉटिंग पैदल-चाल खत्म करने के लिए होते हैं, क्योंकि पैदल चलना पिकिंग के समय का लगभग आधा है और पिकिंग सबसे बड़ी श्रम-लागत है।

segments.src: 3. Automation buys throughput with capital and gives up flexibility — the right level depends on how stable your volume and product mix are.
segments.tr: 3. स्वचालन पूँजी से थ्रूपुट खरीदता है और लचीलापन छोड़ता है — सही स्तर इस पर निर्भर है कि आपकी मात्रा और उत्पाद-मिश्रण कितने स्थिर हैं।

segments.tr: ## ✅ स्व-परीक्षा

segments.tr: A) बारकोड स्कैन करने में

segments.src: Which automation choice generally fits better?

segments.tr: A) पीक के लिए आकार दी गई एक स्थिर कन्वेयर-और-सॉर्टेशन प्रणाली

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 आज के शब्द

segments.src: - **Slotting** — deciding which item goes in which storage location, usually to minimize picker travel.
segments.tr: - **स्लॉटिंग** — तय करना कि कौन-सा सामान किस भंडारण स्थान पर रखा जाए, आम तौर पर चुनने वाले की यात्रा घटाने के लिए।

segments.src: - **ABC analysis** — ranking SKUs by activity (A = fastest moving) so storage and effort go where the volume is.
segments.tr: - **ABC विश्लेषण** — SKU को गतिविधि के आधार पर क्रमबद्ध करना (A = सबसे तेज़ चलने वाला) ताकि भंडारण और मेहनत वहाँ लगे जहाँ मात्रा है।

segments.src: - **Batch picking** — picking items for multiple orders in a single trip through the warehouse, then sorting them by order afterward.
segments.tr: - **बैच पिकिंग** — एक ही चक्कर में गोदाम से गुज़रते हुए कई ऑर्डरों के सामान उठाना, और बाद में उन्हें ऑर्डर के अनुसार छाँटना।

segments.src: - **Goods-to-person (G2P)** — automation that brings inventory to a stationary worker instead of sending the worker to the inventory.
segments.tr: - **Goods-to-person (G2P)** — ऐसा स्वचालन जो कर्मचारी को भंडार तक भेजने के बजाय भंडार को एक स्थिर कर्मचारी तक लाता है।

segments.src: - **Cross-docking** — moving freight straight from an inbound trailer to an outbound one with little or no storage in between.
segments.tr: - **Cross-docking** — आने वाले ट्रेलर से माल को बीच में बहुत कम या बिना भंडारण के सीधे जाने वाले ट्रेलर में भेजना।

segments.src: *Answers: **1) B** — travel typically accounts for around half of order-picking time in manual operations, which is why layout and slotting matter so much.
segments.tr: *उत्तर: **1) B** — मैनुअल ऑर्डर-पिकिंग में यात्रा आम तौर पर लगभग आधा समय लेती है, इसीलिए लेआउट और स्लॉटिंग इतने मायने रखते हैं।

segments.src: **2) O (True)** — slotting fast movers into the golden zone near pack-out shortens both walking and reaching.
segments.tr: **2) O (सही)** — गोल्डन ज़ोन में पैक-आउट के पास तेज़ चलने वाले सामान की स्लॉटिंग पैदल चलना और पहुँचना, दोनों घटाती है।

segments.src: **3) B** — AMRs scale incrementally and tolerate a changing SKU mix; fixed conveyor and AS/RS deliver higher throughput but lock in a layout and need stable, predictable volume to justify the payback period.*

es.title: [Logística 101 #7] El edificio que decide si tu pedido llega mañana

segments.src: > A warehouse isn't a place to park boxes — it's a machine for turning space, walking distance, and labor into delivery speed.
segments.tr: > Un almacén no es un lugar donde guardar cajas, sino una máquina que convierte espacio, distancia a pie y mano de obra en velocidad de entrega.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concepto de hoy

segments.src: Say "warehouse" and most people picture shelves.
segments.tr: Al decir "almacén", la mayoría imagina estanterías.

segments.src: In supply chain terms, though, a warehouse is a decision stack: four choices that together determine how fast and how cheaply an order gets out the door.
segments.tr: Sin embargo, en términos de cadena de suministro, un almacén es una pila de decisiones: cuatro elecciones que, juntas, determinan qué tan rápido y qué tan barato sale un pedido por la puerta.

segments.src: Siting — where do you put the building?**
segments.tr: Ubicación: ¿dónde se construye el edificio?**

segments.src: Every location is a tug-of-war.
segments.tr: Cada ubicación es un tira y afloja.

segments.src: Sit close to your customers and outbound delivery gets cheap and fast, but land and labor cost more.
segments.tr: Si está cerca de los clientes, la entrega saliente es barata y rápida, pero el terreno y la mano de obra cuestan más.

segments.src: Sit close to the port or the factory and inbound freight gets cheap, but every order travels farther.
segments.tr: Si está cerca del puerto o de la fábrica, el flete entrante es barato, pero cada pedido recorre más distancia.

segments.src: Planners also weigh labor availability (can you actually hire 400 people in November?), highway and rail access, property taxes, and how many other companies are already bidding for the same workers.
segments.tr: Los planificadores también evalúan la disponibilidad de mano de obra (¿realmente se pueden contratar 400 personas en noviembre?), el acceso a autopistas y ferrocarril, los impuestos sobre la propiedad y cuántas otras empresas ya compiten por los mismos trabajadores.

segments.src: A common starting tool is the **center of gravity method**: plot demand on a map, weight each point by volume, and find the balance point.
segments.tr: Una herramienta inicial común es el **método del centro de gravedad**: se ubica la demanda en un mapa, se pondera cada punto según su volumen y se busca el punto de equilibrio.

segments.src: It's a first draft, not an answer — the real site has to have power, a highway ramp, and people.
segments.tr: Es un primer borrador, no una respuesta: el sitio real debe tener energía, un acceso a la autopista y personas.

segments.src: Layout — how does product flow through it?**
segments.tr: Distribución: ¿cómo fluye el producto por el edificio?**

segments.src: Goods generally move: receiving → putaway → storage → picking → packing → shipping.
segments.tr: Las mercancías normalmente se mueven así: recepción → ubicación en almacenamiento → almacenamiento → preparación de pedidos (picking) → embalaje → envío.

segments.src: The layout's job is to make that path short and keep flows from crossing.
segments.tr: La función de la distribución es acortar ese recorrido y evitar que los flujos se crucen.

segments.src: Two classic shapes:
segments.tr: Dos formas clásicas:

segments.src: - **I-flow (through-flow):** docks on opposite ends, product moves straight across. Simple, good for high-volume, cross-dock-heavy operations.
segments.tr: - **Flujo en I (flujo directo):** los muelles están en extremos opuestos y el producto cruza en línea recta. Es simple y adecuado para operaciones de alto volumen con mucho cross-docking.

segments.src: - **U-flow:** receiving and shipping on the same wall. Fast-moving items sit near that wall so they're close to both, and one dock crew can flex between inbound and outbound.
segments.tr: - **Flujo en U:** recepción y envío en la misma pared. Los artículos de rotación rápida se colocan cerca de esa pared para estar cerca de ambos, y un mismo equipo de muelle puede alternar entre entrada y salida.

segments.src: Picking — where the labor actually goes.**
segments.tr: Preparación de pedidos (picking): donde realmente se va la mano de obra.**

segments.src: Order picking is typically the single largest labor line in a distribution center, and in manual operations, studies consistently find that *walking* eats roughly half of a picker's time.
segments.tr: La preparación de pedidos suele ser la partida de mano de obra más grande de un centro de distribución y, en operaciones manuales, los estudios coinciden en que *caminar* consume aproximadamente la mitad del tiempo de un preparador.

segments.src: That's why almost every improvement idea is really a walking-reduction idea:
segments.tr: Por eso casi toda mejora es, en realidad, una idea para reducir la caminata:

segments.src: - **Slotting:** put the fast movers in the "golden zone" (waist-to-shoulder height, near the pack stations) and the slow movers up high or far back. Usually driven by **ABC analysis** — the top ~20% of SKUs often drive ~80% of the picks.
segments.tr: - **Slotting (asignación de ubicaciones):** coloque los artículos de rotación rápida en la "zona dorada" (entre la cintura y los hombros, cerca de las estaciones de embalaje) y los de rotación lenta arriba o al fondo. Normalmente se guía con un **análisis ABC**: el 20 % superior de los SKU suele generar el 80 % de las preparaciones.

segments.src: - **Batch picking:** grab items for 12 orders in one trip instead of walking the aisle 12 times.
segments.tr: - **Preparación por lotes (batch picking):** tomar artículos de 12 pedidos en un solo recorrido en lugar de recorrer el pasillo 12 veces.

segments.src: - **Zone picking:** each worker owns one area; totes move between zones by conveyor.
segments.tr: - **Preparación por zonas (zone picking):** cada trabajador se encarga de un área; las cajas se mueven entre zonas por transportador.

segments.src: - **Goods-to-person:** stop walking entirely — bring the shelf to the human.
segments.tr: - **Mercancía hacia la persona (goods-to-person):** dejar de caminar por completo: llevar la estantería hasta la persona.

segments.src: Automation — how much steel do you buy?**
segments.tr: Automatización: ¿cuánto acero se compra?**

segments.src: The menu runs from cheap and flexible to expensive and fast: barcode scanners → pick-to-light and voice picking → conveyors and sorters → **AMRs** (mobile robots that carry totes or whole shelving pods) → **AS/RS** (automated storage and retrieval systems: cranes or shuttles in dense racking).
segments.tr: El menú va desde lo barato y flexible hasta lo caro y rápido: lectores de códigos de barras → preparación con luz indicadora y por voz → transportadores y clasificadoras → **AMR** (robots móviles que transportan cajas o módulos completos de estantería) → **AS/RS** (sistemas automatizados de almacenamiento y recuperación: grúas o lanzaderas en estanterías densas).

segments.src: The trade-off is blunt:
segments.tr: El compromiso es directo:

segments.src: fixed automation  = high throughput, low flexibility, long payback (often 5-10 years)
segments.tr: fixed automation  = high throughput, low flexibility, long payback (often 5-10 years)

segments.src: mobile robots     = lower throughput per unit, but you can add or remove them
segments.tr: mobile robots     = lower throughput per unit, but you can add or remove them

segments.src: Fixed conveyor is poured concrete — great if your volume and product mix are stable for a decade.
segments.tr: El transportador fijo es como concreto colado: excelente si el volumen y la mezcla de productos se mantienen estables durante una década.

segments.src: If your SKU mix changes every season, that steel becomes a cage.
segments.tr: Si la mezcla de SKU cambia cada temporada, ese acero se convierte en una jaula.

segments.src: And none of it works without a **WMS** (warehouse management system) telling everyone and everything where to go.
segments.tr: Y nada de esto funciona sin un **WMS** (sistema de gestión de almacenes) que indique a todos y a todo dónde debe ir.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## En la vida cotidiana

segments.src: You order a phone case at 11 p.m.
segments.tr: Pides una funda para el teléfono a las 11 p. m.

segments.src: on a Tuesday and it's on your porch Thursday morning.
segments.tr: un martes y llega a tu porche el jueves por la mañana.

segments.src: Here's what those four decisions did for you.
segments.tr: Esto es lo que hicieron esas cuatro decisiones por ti.

segments.src: **Siting:** the item shipped from a fulfillment center outside Columbus, Ohio — one of the most crowded distribution corridors in the country, along with Indianapolis, Memphis, and California's Inland Empire.
segments.tr: **Ubicación:** el artículo se envió desde un centro de cumplimiento a las afueras de Columbus, Ohio, uno de los corredores de distribución más congestionados del país, junto con Indianápolis, Memphis y el Inland Empire de California.

segments.src: Central Ohio is popular partly because a single day's truck drive from there reaches a very large share of the U.S.
segments.tr: El centro de Ohio es popular en parte porque un solo día de viaje en camión desde allí llega a una gran parte de la

segments.src: population.
segments.tr: población de EE. UU.

segments.src: The company paid for that: industrial space is quoted in dollars per square foot per year, and rents run from the high single digits in parts of the Midwest to well into the teens and above in Southern California.
segments.tr: La empresa pagó por eso: el espacio industrial se cotiza en dólares por pie cuadrado al año, y los alquileres van desde unos 8 o 9 dólares en algunas zonas del Medio Oeste hasta 15 dólares o más en el sur de California.

segments.src: That premium buys a delivery promise.
segments.tr: Esa prima compra una promesa de entrega.

segments.src: **Layout and slotting:** your case wasn't stored next to other phone cases.
segments.tr: **Distribución y asignación de ubicaciones:** tu funda no se almacenó junto a otras fundas.

segments.src: Many large fulfillment centers use *random* (sometimes called chaotic) storage — items go wherever there's an open bin, and the WMS remembers.
segments.tr: Muchos centros de cumplimiento grandes usan almacenamiento *aleatorio* (a veces llamado caótico): los artículos van a cualquier contenedor libre, y el WMS lo recuerda.

segments.src: It sounds like chaos; it's actually better cube utilization and shorter walks, because popular items end up scattered near many pick paths instead of clustered in one aisle everyone has to visit.
segments.tr: Suena a caos; en realidad significa mejor aprovechamiento del cubo y recorridos más cortos, porque los artículos populares quedan dispersos cerca de muchas rutas de preparación en lugar de agruparse en un solo pasillo que todos deben visitar.

segments.src: **Picking:** a worker pushing a cart of totes picked your case as part of a batch of 20-some orders, guided by a handheld that sequenced the route.
segments.tr: **Preparación:** un trabajador empujando un carro de cajas recogió tu funda como parte de un lote de unos 20 pedidos, guiado por un dispositivo portátil que ordenaba la ruta.

segments.src: Or a robot drove a whole shelving pod to a stationary picker who never took a step.
segments.tr: O un robot condujo un módulo completo de estantería hasta un preparador fijo que nunca dio un paso.

segments.src: **Automation:** at pack-out, your box hit a conveyor, got weighed (a weight mismatch flags a wrong-item pick), passed a scanner, and a sorter diverted it down the chute for the right carrier trailer.
segments.tr: **Automatización:** en el embalaje, tu caja llegó a un transportador, se pesó (una discrepancia de peso indica un artículo equivocado), pasó por un lector y un clasificador la desvió por el canal hacia el remolque del transportista correcto.

segments.src: That trailer left on a scheduled cutoff — miss the cutoff and "Thursday" becomes "Friday."
segments.tr: Ese remolque salió según un horario de corte; si se pierde el corte, el "jueves" se convierte en "viernes".

segments.src: Which is the real lesson: the delivery date you saw at checkout was mostly decided by a building's floor plan and a truck's departure time.
segments.tr: Y esa es la verdadera lección: la fecha de entrega que viste al pagar la decidieron sobre todo la distribución de un edificio y la hora de salida de un camión.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Resumen en tres líneas

segments.src: 1. Warehouse siting trades outbound speed and cost against land, labor, and inbound freight — you can't optimize all of them.
segments.tr: 1. La ubicación del almacén equilibra la velocidad y el costo de salida frente al terreno, la mano de obra y el flete de entrada; no se pueden optimizar todos a la vez.

segments.src: 2. Layout and slotting exist to kill walking, because walking is roughly half of picking time and picking is the biggest labor cost.
segments.tr: 2. La distribución y la asignación de ubicaciones existen para eliminar la caminata, porque caminar es aproximadamente la mitad del tiempo de preparación y la preparación es el mayor costo de mano de obra.

segments.src: 3. Automation buys throughput with capital and gives up flexibility — the right level depends on how stable your volume and product mix are.
segments.tr: 3. La automatización compra capacidad de procesamiento con capital y renuncia a flexibilidad; el nivel adecuado depende de cuán estables sean tu volumen y tu mezcla de productos.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Autoevaluación

segments.src: **1.** In a typical manual, picker-to-goods operation, the largest single chunk of a picker's time goes to:
segments.tr: **1.** En una operación manual típica de preparación (preparador hacia la mercancía), la mayor parte del tiempo del preparador se destina a:

segments.src: A) scanning barcodes
segments.tr: A) escanear códigos de barras

segments.src: B) traveling (walking) between locations
segments.tr: B) desplazarse (caminar) entre ubicaciones

segments.src: C) packing cartons
segments.tr: C) empacar cajas

segments.src: D) waiting for a forklift
segments.tr: D) esperar un montacargas

segments.src: **2.** (O/X) Placing your fastest-moving SKUs at waist height near the pack stations is called *slotting*, and its main purpose is to reduce travel time.
segments.tr: **2.** (O/X) Colocar tus SKU de rotación más rápida a la altura de la cintura, cerca de las estaciones de embalaje, se llama *slotting*, y su objetivo principal es reducir el tiempo de desplazamiento.

segments.src: **3.** A retailer's volume triples every Q4 and its product mix changes every season.
segments.tr: **3.** El volumen de un minorista se triplica cada cuarto trimestre y su mezcla de productos cambia cada temporada.

segments.src: Which automation choice generally fits better?
segments.tr: ¿Qué opción de automatización se ajusta mejor en general?

segments.src: A) A fixed conveyor-and-sortation system sized for peak
segments.tr: A) Un sistema fijo de transportadores y clasificación dimensionado para el pico

segments.src: B) Mobile robots (AMRs) that can be added or removed as volume changes
segments.tr: B) Robots móviles (AMR) que pueden añadirse o retirarse según cambie el volumen

segments.src: C) A full AS/RS crane system
segments.tr: C) Un sistema completo de grúas AS/RS

segments.src: D) No technology at all
segments.tr: D) Sin ninguna tecnología

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Términos de hoy

segments.src: - **Slotting** — deciding which item goes in which storage location, usually to minimize picker travel.
segments.tr: - **Slotting (asignación de ubicaciones)**: decidir qué artículo va en qué ubicación de almacenamiento, normalmente para minimizar el desplazamiento del preparador.

segments.src: - **ABC analysis** — ranking SKUs by activity (A = fastest moving) so storage and effort go where the volume is.
segments.tr: - **Análisis ABC**: clasificar los SKU por actividad (A = de rotación más rápida) para que el almacenamiento y el esfuerzo se concentren donde está el volumen.

segments.src: - **Batch picking** — picking items for multiple orders in a single trip through the warehouse, then sorting them by order afterward.
segments.tr: - **Preparación por lotes (batch picking)**: preparar artículos de varios pedidos en un solo recorrido por el almacén y luego separarlos por pedido.

segments.src: - **Goods-to-person (G2P)** — automation that brings inventory to a stationary worker instead of sending the worker to the inventory.
segments.tr: - **Mercancía hacia la persona (G2P)**: automatización que lleva el inventario a un trabajador fijo en lugar de enviar al trabajador al inventario.

segments.src: - **Cross-docking** — moving freight straight from an inbound trailer to an outbound one with little or no storage in between.
segments.tr: - **Cross-docking**: mover la carga directamente de un remolque de entrada a uno de salida, con poco o ningún almacenamiento intermedio.

segments.src: *Answers: **1) B** — travel typically accounts for around half of order-picking time in manual operations, which is why layout and slotting matter so much.
segments.tr: *Respuestas: **1) B**: el desplazamiento suele representar alrededor de la mitad del tiempo de preparación de pedidos en operaciones manuales, por eso la distribución y la asignación de ubicaciones son tan importantes.

segments.src: **2) O (True)** — slotting fast movers into the golden zone near pack-out shortens both walking and reaching.
segments.tr: **2) O (Verdadero)**: colocar los artículos de rotación rápida en la zona dorada, cerca del embalaje, acorta tanto el caminar como el alcance.

segments.src: **3) B** — AMRs scale incrementally and tolerate a changing SKU mix; fixed conveyor and AS/RS deliver higher throughput but lock in a layout and need stable, predictable volume to justify the payback period.*
segments.tr: **3) B**: los AMR escalan gradualmente y toleran una mezcla cambiante de SKU; el transportador fijo y el AS/RS ofrecen mayor capacidad, pero fijan una distribución y requieren volumen estable y predecible para justificar el periodo de recuperación de la inversión.*

segments.tr: - **الالتقاط الدفعي (Batch picking):** التقط أصناف 12 طلبًا في جولة واحدة بدلًا من السير في الممر 12 مرة.

segments.src: - **Zone picking:** each worker owns one area; totes move between zones by conveyor.
segments.tr: - **الالتقاط بالمناطق (Zone picking):** يتولى كل عامل منطقة واحدة، وتنتقل الصناديق بين المناطق عبر السير الناقل.

segments.src: - **Goods-to-person:** stop walking entirely — bring the shelf to the human.
segments.tr: - **البضاعة إلى الشخص (Goods-to-person):** توقف عن المشي كليًا، وأحضر الرف إلى الإنسان.

segments.src: Automation — how much steel do you buy?**
segments.tr: الأتمتة: كم من المعدات الحديدية تشتري؟**

segments.src: The menu runs from cheap and flexible to expensive and fast: barcode scanners → pick-to-light and voice picking → conveyors and sorters → **AMRs** (mobile robots that carry totes or whole shelving pods) → **AS/RS** (automated storage and retrieval systems: cranes or shuttles in dense racking).
segments.tr: تتدرج القائمة من الخيارات الرخيصة والمرنة إلى الخيارات الغالية والسريعة: قارئات الباركود ← الالتقاط بالإشارة الضوئية والالتقاط الصوتي ← السيور الناقلة وأجهزة الفرز ← **AMRs** (روبوتات متنقلة تحمل الصناديق أو وحدات رفوف كاملة) ← **AS/RS** (أنظمة التخزين والاسترجاع الآلية: رافعات أو مكوكات داخل الرفوف الكثيفة).

segments.src: The trade-off is blunt:
segments.tr: المقايضة واضحة:

segments.src: fixed automation  = high throughput, low flexibility, long payback (often 5-10 years)
segments.tr: fixed automation  = high throughput, low flexibility, long payback (often 5-10 years)

segments.src: mobile robots     = lower throughput per unit, but you can add or remove them
segments.tr: mobile robots     = lower throughput per unit, but you can add or remove them

segments.src: Fixed conveyor is poured concrete — great if your volume and product mix are stable for a decade.
segments.tr: السير الناقل الثابت أشبه بالخرسانة المصبوبة، وهو ممتاز إذا كان حجمك ومزيج منتجاتك مستقرين لعقد كامل.

segments.src: If your SKU mix changes every season, that steel becomes a cage.
segments.tr: أما إذا تغيّر مزيج وحدات SKU مع كل موسم، فإن ذلك الحديد يتحول إلى قفص.

segments.src: And none of it works without a **WMS** (warehouse management system) telling everyone and everything where to go.
segments.tr: ولا يعمل أي من ذلك دون **WMS** (نظام إدارة المستودعات) الذي يخبر الجميع وكل شيء أين يذهب.

segments.src: Many large fulfillment centers use *random* (sometimes called chaotic) storage — items go wherever there's an open bin, and the WMS remembers.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap

segments.src: 1. Warehouse siting trades outbound speed and cost against land, labor, and inbound freight — you can't optimize all of them.
segments.tr: 1. يقايض تموضع المستودع السرعة والتكلفة الصادرة بالأراضي والعمالة والشحن الوارد، ولا يمكنك تحسينها كلها معًا.

segments.src: 2. Layout and slotting exist to kill walking, because walking is roughly half of picking time and picking is the biggest labor cost.
segments.tr: 2. وُجد التخطيط وتحديد المواقع للقضاء على المشي، لأن المشي يمثل نحو نصف وقت الالتقاط، والالتقاط هو أكبر تكلفة عمالة.

segments.src: 3. Automation buys throughput with capital and gives up flexibility — the right level depends on how stable your volume and product mix are.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 مصطلحات اليوم

segments.src: - **Slotting** — deciding which item goes in which storage location, usually to minimize picker travel.
segments.tr: - **تحديد المواقع (Slotting)**: تحديد الصنف الذي يوضع في أي موقع تخزين، عادةً لتقليل تنقل العامل.

segments.src: - **ABC analysis** — ranking SKUs by activity (A = fastest moving) so storage and effort go where the volume is.
segments.tr: - **تحليل ABC**: ترتيب وحدات SKU حسب النشاط (A = الأسرع حركة) حتى يُوجَّه التخزين والجهد إلى حيث يوجد الحجم.

segments.src: - **Batch picking** — picking items for multiple orders in a single trip through the warehouse, then sorting them by order afterward.
segments.tr: - **الالتقاط الدفعي (Batch picking)**: التقاط أصناف لعدة طلبات في جولة واحدة عبر المستودع، ثم فرزها حسب الطلب لاحقًا.

segments.src: - **Goods-to-person (G2P)** — automation that brings inventory to a stationary worker instead of sending the worker to the inventory.
segments.tr: - **البضاعة إلى الشخص (Goods-to-person / G2P)**: أتمتة تُحضر المخزون إلى عامل ثابت بدلًا من إرسال العامل إلى المخزون.

segments.src: - **Cross-docking** — moving freight straight from an inbound trailer to an outbound one with little or no storage in between.
segments.tr: - **العبور المباشر (Cross-docking)**: نقل البضائع مباشرة من شاحنة واردة إلى شاحنة صادرة مع تخزين قليل جدًا أو معدوم بينهما.

segments.src: *Answers: **1) B** — travel typically accounts for around half of order-picking time in manual operations, which is why layout and slotting matter so much.
segments.tr: *الإجابات: **1) B** — يمثل التنقل عادةً نحو نصف وقت التقاط الطلبات في العمليات اليدوية، ولهذا يكتسب التخطيط وتحديد المواقع أهمية كبيرة.

segments.src: **2) O (True)** — slotting fast movers into the golden zone near pack-out shortens both walking and reaching.
segments.tr: **2) O (صحيح)** — وضع الأصناف سريعة الحركة في المنطقة الذهبية قرب التغليف يقصّر المشي والوصول معًا.

segments.src: **3) B** — AMRs scale incrementally and tolerate a changing SKU mix; fixed conveyor and AS/RS deliver higher throughput but lock in a layout and need stable, predictable volume to justify the payback period.*
segments.tr: **3) B** — تتوسع الروبوتات AMRs تدريجيًا وتتحمل تغيّر مزيج SKU، أما السير الثابت وAS/RS فيحققان إنتاجية أعلى لكنهما يثبتان التخطيط ويحتاجان إلى حجم مستقر ويمكن التنبؤ به لتبرير فترة استرداد الاستثمار.*

fr.title: [Logistique 101 n°7] Le bâtiment qui décide si votre commande arrive demain

segments.src: > A warehouse isn't a place to park boxes — it's a machine for turning space, walking distance, and labor into delivery speed.
segments.tr: > Un entrepôt n'est pas un endroit où entreposer des cartons — c'est une machine qui transforme l'espace, la distance à parcourir et la main-d'œuvre en rapidité de livraison.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concept du jour

segments.src: Say "warehouse" and most people picture shelves.
segments.tr: Quand on dit « entrepôt », la plupart des gens imaginent des étagères.

segments.src: In supply chain terms, though, a warehouse is a decision stack: four choices that together determine how fast and how cheaply an order gets out the door.
segments.tr: Dans les termes de la chaîne d'approvisionnement, cependant, un entrepôt est un ensemble de décisions : quatre choix qui déterminent ensemble la vitesse et le coût avec lesquels une commande sort.

segments.src: Siting — where do you put the building?**
segments.tr: Implantation — où placer le bâtiment ?**

segments.src: Every location is a tug-of-war.
segments.tr: Chaque emplacement est un bras de fer.

segments.src: Sit close to your customers and outbound delivery gets cheap and fast, but land and labor cost more.
segments.tr: Situé près de vos clients, l'expédition devient peu coûteuse et rapide, mais le foncier et la main-d'œuvre coûtent plus cher.

segments.src: Sit close to the port or the factory and inbound freight gets cheap, but every order travels farther.
segments.tr: Situé près du port ou de l'usine, le fret entrant est bon marché, mais chaque commande parcourt une plus grande distance.

segments.src: Planners also weigh labor availability (can you actually hire 400 people in November?), highway and rail access, property taxes, and how many other companies are already bidding for the same workers.
segments.tr: Les planificateurs pèsent aussi la disponibilité de la main-d'œuvre (peut-on vraiment recruter 400 personnes en novembre ?), l'accès aux autoroutes et au rail, la fiscalité foncière, et le nombre d'autres entreprises qui se disputent les mêmes salariés.

segments.src: A common starting tool is the **center of gravity method**: plot demand on a map, weight each point by volume, and find the balance point.
segments.tr: Un outil de départ courant est la **méthode du centre de gravité** : on place la demande sur une carte, on pondère chaque point par son volume, et on cherche le point d'équilibre.

segments.src: It's a first draft, not an answer — the real site has to have power, a highway ramp, and people.
segments.tr: C'est un premier brouillon, pas une réponse — le site réel doit disposer d'électricité, d'un accès à l'autoroute et de main-d'œuvre.

segments.src: Layout — how does product flow through it?**
segments.tr: Agencement — comment les produits y circulent-ils ?**

segments.src: Goods generally move: receiving → putaway → storage → picking → packing → shipping.
segments.tr: Les marchandises suivent généralement ce cheminement : réception → rangement → stockage → préparation → emballage → expédition.

segments.src: The layout's job is to make that path short and keep flows from crossing.
segments.tr: Le rôle de l'agencement est de raccourcir ce parcours et d'éviter que les flux se croisent.

segments.src: Two classic shapes:
segments.tr: Deux formes classiques :

segments.src: - **I-flow (through-flow):** docks on opposite ends, product moves straight across. Simple, good for high-volume, cross-dock-heavy operations.
segments.tr: - **Flux en I (flux traversant) :** les quais sont situés aux deux extrémités et les produits traversent le bâtiment en ligne droite. Simple, adapté aux opérations à fort volume et à forte part de cross-docking.

segments.src: - **U-flow:** receiving and shipping on the same wall. Fast-moving items sit near that wall so they're close to both, and one dock crew can flex between inbound and outbound.
segments.tr: - **Flux en U :** réception et expédition sont sur le même mur. Les articles à rotation rapide sont placés près de ce mur, donc proches des deux fonctions, et une même équipe de quai peut passer de l'entrée à la sortie selon les besoins.

segments.src: Picking — where the labor actually goes.**
segments.tr: Préparation — là où va réellement la main-d'œuvre.**

segments.src: Order picking is typically the single largest labor line in a distribution center, and in manual operations, studies consistently find that *walking* eats roughly half of a picker's time.
segments.tr: La préparation des commandes est généralement le premier poste de main-d'œuvre d'un centre de distribution, et dans les opérations manuelles, les études constatent systématiquement que *la marche* absorbe environ la moitié du temps d'un préparateur.

segments.src: That's why almost every improvement idea is really a walking-reduction idea:
segments.tr: C'est pourquoi presque toutes les idées d'amélioration relèvent en fait de la réduction des déplacements :

segments.src: - **Slotting:** put the fast movers in the "golden zone" (waist-to-shoulder height, near the pack stations) and the slow movers up high or far back. Usually driven by **ABC analysis** — the top ~20% of SKUs often drive ~80% of the picks.
segments.tr: - **Slotting (affectation des emplacements) :** placer les articles à rotation rapide dans la « zone dorée » (entre la taille et l'épaule), près des postes d'emballage, et les articles lents en hauteur ou au fond. Il repose généralement sur une **analyse ABC** : les 20 % de références les plus actives génèrent souvent 80 % des prélèvements.

segments.src: - **Batch picking:** grab items for 12 orders in one trip instead of walking the aisle 12 times.
segments.tr: - **Préparation par lots :** prélever les articles de 12 commandes en un seul passage, au lieu de parcourir l'allée 12 fois.

segments.src: - **Zone picking:** each worker owns one area; totes move between zones by conveyor.
segments.tr: - **Préparation par zones :** chaque préparateur gère une zone ; les bacs passent d'une zone à l'autre par convoyeur.

segments.src: - **Goods-to-person:** stop walking entirely — bring the shelf to the human.
segments.tr: - **Marchandises vers l'opérateur (goods-to-person) :** plus aucune marche — on amène l'étagère à la personne.

segments.src: Automation — how much steel do you buy?**
segments.tr: Automatisation — combien d'équipement acheter ?**

segments.src: The menu runs from cheap and flexible to expensive and fast: barcode scanners → pick-to-light and voice picking → conveyors and sorters → **AMRs** (mobile robots that carry totes or whole shelving pods) → **AS/RS** (automated storage and retrieval systems: cranes or shuttles in dense racking).
segments.tr: L'éventail va de solutions peu coûteuses et flexibles à des solutions onéreuses et rapides : scanners de codes-barres → préparation assistée par voix ou par témoins lumineux → convoyeurs et trieurs → **AMR** (robots mobiles qui transportent des bacs ou des racks entiers) → **AS/RS** (systèmes automatisés de stockage et de déstockage : grues ou navettes dans des rayonnages denses).

segments.src: The trade-off is blunt:
segments.tr: Le compromis est simple :

segments.src: fixed automation  = high throughput, low flexibility, long payback (often 5-10 years)
segments.tr: fixed automation  = high throughput, low flexibility, long payback (often 5-10 years)

segments.src: mobile robots     = lower throughput per unit, but you can add or remove them
segments.tr: mobile robots     = lower throughput per unit, but you can add or remove them

segments.src: Fixed conveyor is poured concrete — great if your volume and product mix are stable for a decade.
segments.tr: Un convoyeur fixe, c'est du béton coulé — parfait si vos volumes et votre gamme restent stables pendant une décennie.

segments.src: If your SKU mix changes every season, that steel becomes a cage.
segments.tr: Si votre assortiment change à chaque saison, cet investissement devient une cage.

segments.src: And none of it works without a **WMS** (warehouse management system) telling everyone and everything where to go.
segments.tr: Et rien de tout cela ne fonctionne sans un **WMS** (système de gestion d'entrepôt) qui indique à chacun, et à chaque équipement, où aller.
