pt.title: [Logística 101 #7] O Prédio que Decide se o Seu Pedido Chega Amanhã

segments.src: > A warehouse isn't a place to park boxes — it's a machine for turning space, walking distance, and labor into delivery speed.
segments.tr: > Um armazém não é um lugar para estacionar caixas — é uma máquina que transforma espaço, distância a pé e mão de obra em velocidade de entrega.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Conceito de Hoje

segments.src: Say "warehouse" and most people picture shelves.
segments.tr: Diga "armazém" e a maioria das pessoas imagina prateleiras.

segments.src: In supply chain terms, though, a warehouse is a decision stack: four choices that together determine how fast and how cheaply an order gets out the door.
segments.tr: No termo da cadeia de suprimentos, porém, um armazém é uma pilha de decisões: quatro escolhas que, juntas, determinam a rapidez e o custo com que um pedido sai pela porta.

segments.src: Siting — where do you put the building?**
segments.tr: Localização — onde você coloca o prédio?**

segments.src: Every location is a tug-of-war.
segments.tr: Cada localização é um cabo de guerra.

segments.src: Sit close to your customers and outbound delivery gets cheap and fast, but land and labor cost more.
segments.tr: Ficar perto dos clientes torna a entrega de saída barata e rápida, mas o terreno e a mão de obra custam mais.

segments.src: Sit close to the port or the factory and inbound freight gets cheap, but every order travels farther.
segments.tr: Ficar perto do porto ou da fábrica torna o frete de entrada barato, mas cada pedido percorre uma distância maior.

segments.src: Planners also weigh labor availability (can you actually hire 400 people in November?), highway and rail access, property taxes, and how many other companies are already bidding for the same workers.
segments.tr: Os planejadores também avaliam a disponibilidade de mão de obra (você consegue contratar 400 pessoas em novembro?), o acesso a rodovias e ferrovias, os impostos sobre a propriedade e quantas outras empresas já disputam os mesmos trabalhadores.

segments.src: A common starting tool is the **center of gravity method**: plot demand on a map, weight each point by volume, and find the balance point.
segments.tr: Um ponto de partida comum é o **método do centro de gravidade**: plotar a demanda em um mapa, ponderar cada ponto pelo volume e encontrar o ponto de equilíbrio.

segments.src: It's a first draft, not an answer — the real site has to have power, a highway ramp, and people.
segments.tr: É um rascunho, não uma resposta — o local real precisa ter energia, acesso à rodovia e mão de obra.

segments.src: Layout — how does product flow through it?**
segments.tr: Layout — como o produto flui por ele?**

segments.src: Goods generally move: receiving → putaway → storage → picking → packing → shipping.
segments.tr: As mercadorias geralmente seguem: recebimento → endereçamento → armazenagem → separação → embalagem → expedição.

segments.src: The layout's job is to make that path short and keep flows from crossing.
segments.tr: A função do layout é tornar esse caminho curto e evitar que os fluxos se cruzem.

segments.src: Two classic shapes:
segments.tr: Dois formatos clássicos:

segments.src: - **I-flow (through-flow):** docks on opposite ends, product moves straight across. Simple, good for high-volume, cross-dock-heavy operations.
segments.tr: - **Fluxo em I (fluxo contínuo):** as docas ficam em extremos opostos, e o produto atravessa em linha reta. Simples, bom para operações de alto volume e com muito cross-docking.

segments.src: - **U-flow:** receiving and shipping on the same wall. Fast-moving items sit near that wall so they're close to both, and one dock crew can flex between inbound and outbound.
segments.tr: - **Fluxo em U:** recebimento e expedição na mesma parede. Os itens de giro rápido ficam perto dessa parede, para estarem próximos de ambos, e uma mesma equipe de doca pode alternar entre entrada e saída.

segments.src: Picking — where the labor actually goes.**
segments.tr: Separação — onde a mão de obra realmente vai.**

segments.src: Order picking is typically the single largest labor line in a distribution center, and in manual operations, studies consistently find that *walking* eats roughly half of a picker's time.
segments.tr: A separação de pedidos costuma ser a maior linha de custo de mão de obra em um centro de distribuição e, em operações manuais, estudos encontram de forma consistente que *andar* consome cerca de metade do tempo do separador.

segments.src: That's why almost every improvement idea is really a walking-reduction idea:
segments.tr: Por isso, quase toda ideia de melhoria é, na prática, uma ideia de redução de deslocamento:

segments.src: - **Slotting:** put the fast movers in the "golden zone" (waist-to-shoulder height, near the pack stations) and the slow movers up high or far back. Usually driven by **ABC analysis** — the top ~20% of SKUs often drive ~80% of the picks.
segments.tr: - **Slotting:** coloque os itens de giro rápido na "zona dourada" (altura da cintura até os ombros, perto das estações de embalagem) e os de giro lento no alto ou no fundo. Normalmente guiado pela **análise ABC** — os cerca de 20% principais SKUs costumam gerar cerca de 80% das separações.

segments.src: - **Batch picking:** grab items for 12 orders in one trip instead of walking the aisle 12 times.
segments.tr: - **Separação em lote:** pegue os itens de 12 pedidos em uma única viagem, em vez de percorrer o corredor 12 vezes.

segments.src: - **Zone picking:** each worker owns one area; totes move between zones by conveyor.
segments.tr: - **Separação por zona:** cada trabalhador é responsável por uma área; as caixas plásticas (totes) se movem entre as zonas por esteira.

segments.src: - **Goods-to-person:** stop walking entirely — bring the shelf to the human.
segments.tr: - **Goods-to-person:** deixe de andar completamente — leve a prateleira até a pessoa.

segments.src: Automation — how much steel do you buy?**
segments.tr: Automação — quanto aço você vai comprar?**

segments.src: The menu runs from cheap and flexible to expensive and fast: barcode scanners → pick-to-light and voice picking → conveyors and sorters → **AMRs** (mobile robots that carry totes or whole shelving pods) → **AS/RS** (automated storage and retrieval systems: cranes or shuttles in dense racking).
segments.tr: O cardápio vai do barato e flexível ao caro e rápido: leitores de código de barras → pick-to-light e separação por voz → esteiras e separadoras → **AMRs** (robôs móveis que transportam caixas ou módulos inteiros de prateleiras) → **AS/RS** (sistemas automatizados de armazenagem e recuperação: transelevadores ou shuttles em estantes densas).

segments.src: The trade-off is blunt:
segments.tr: A troca é direta:

segments.src: fixed automation  = high throughput, low flexibility, long payback (often 5-10 years)
segments.tr: fixed automation  = high throughput, low flexibility, long payback (often 5-10 years)

segments.src: mobile robots     = lower throughput per unit, but you can add or remove them
segments.tr: mobile robots     = lower throughput per unit, but you can add or remove them

segments.src: Fixed conveyor is poured concrete — great if your volume and product mix are stable for a decade.
segments.tr: Uma esteira fixa é como concreto armado — ótima se o seu volume e o mix de produtos forem estáveis por uma década.

segments.src: If your SKU mix changes every season, that steel becomes a cage.
segments.tr: Se o mix de SKUs mudar a cada temporada, esse aço vira uma gaiola.

segments.src: And none of it works without a **WMS** (warehouse management system) telling everyone and everything where to go.
segments.tr: E nada disso funciona sem um **WMS** (sistema de gerenciamento de armazém) dizendo a todas as pessoas e a todos os equipamentos para onde ir.

segments.tr: **3) B** — os AMRs escalam gradualmente e toleram um mix de SKUs em mudança; esteiras fixas e AS/RS entregam maior capacidade, mas travam um layout e precisam de volume estável e previsível para justificar o prazo de retorno.*

in.title: [Logistik 101 #7] Gudang yang Menentukan Apakah Pesanan Anda Sampai Besok

segments.src: > A warehouse isn't a place to park boxes — it's a machine for turning space, walking distance, and labor into delivery speed.
segments.tr: > Gudang bukan tempat untuk menumpuk kardus — melainkan mesin yang mengubah ruang, jarak tempuh, dan tenaga kerja menjadi kecepatan pengiriman.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Konsep Hari Ini

segments.src: Say "warehouse" and most people picture shelves.
segments.tr: Ketika orang mendengar kata "gudang", kebanyakan membayangkan rak-rak.

segments.src: In supply chain terms, though, a warehouse is a decision stack: four choices that together determine how fast and how cheaply an order gets out the door.
segments.tr: Namun dalam istilah rantai pasok, gudang adalah tumpukan keputusan: empat pilihan yang bersama-sama menentukan seberapa cepat dan seberapa murah sebuah pesanan bisa keluar dari pintu.

segments.src: Siting — where do you put the building?**
segments.tr: Penempatan lokasi — di mana gedung itu dibangun?**

segments.src: Every location is a tug-of-war.
segments.tr: Setiap lokasi adalah tarik-menarik.

segments.src: Sit close to your customers and outbound delivery gets cheap and fast, but land and labor cost more.
segments.tr: Berada dekat dengan pelanggan membuat pengiriman keluar menjadi murah dan cepat, tetapi harga tanah dan tenaga kerja lebih mahal.

segments.src: Sit close to the port or the factory and inbound freight gets cheap, but every order travels farther.
segments.tr: Berada dekat pelabuhan atau pabrik membuat pengiriman masuk menjadi murah, tetapi setiap pesanan menempuh jarak yang lebih jauh.

segments.src: Planners also weigh labor availability (can you actually hire 400 people in November?), highway and rail access, property taxes, and how many other companies are already bidding for the same workers.
segments.tr: Perencana juga menimbang ketersediaan tenaga kerja (apakah Anda benar-benar bisa merekrut 400 orang di bulan November?), akses jalan raya dan rel kereta, pajak properti, serta berapa banyak perusahaan lain yang sudah bersaing memperebutkan pekerja yang sama.

segments.src: A common starting tool is the **center of gravity method**: plot demand on a map, weight each point by volume, and find the balance point.
segments.tr: Alat awal yang umum digunakan adalah **metode pusat gravitasi**: petakan permintaan di peta, beri bobot setiap titik berdasarkan volume, lalu temukan titik keseimbangannya.

segments.src: It's a first draft, not an answer — the real site has to have power, a highway ramp, and people.
segments.tr: Ini hanyalah draf awal, bukan jawaban — lokasi sebenarnya harus memiliki listrik, akses tol, dan tenaga kerja.

segments.src: Layout — how does product flow through it?**
segments.tr: Tata letak — bagaimana produk mengalir di dalamnya?**

segments.src: Goods generally move: receiving → putaway → storage → picking → packing → shipping.
segments.tr: Barang pada umumnya bergerak: penerimaan → penempatan ke rak → penyimpanan → pengambilan → pengemasan → pengiriman.

segments.src: The layout's job is to make that path short and keep flows from crossing.
segments.tr: Tugas tata letak adalah membuat jalur ini pendek dan mencegah aliran barang saling bersilangan.

segments.src: Two classic shapes:
segments.tr: Dua bentuk klasik:

segments.src: - **I-flow (through-flow):** docks on opposite ends, product moves straight across. Simple, good for high-volume, cross-dock-heavy operations.
segments.tr: - **Aliran I (through-flow):** dok berada di kedua ujung yang berlawanan, produk bergerak lurus melintasi gudang. Sederhana, cocok untuk operasi bervolume tinggi yang banyak menggunakan cross-dock.

segments.src: - **U-flow:** receiving and shipping on the same wall. Fast-moving items sit near that wall so they're close to both, and one dock crew can flex between inbound and outbound.
segments.tr: - **Aliran U:** penerimaan dan pengiriman berada di dinding yang sama. Barang yang bergerak cepat ditempatkan dekat dinding tersebut sehingga dekat dengan keduanya, dan satu tim dok bisa bergantian antara barang masuk dan keluar.

segments.src: Picking — where the labor actually goes.**
segments.tr: Pengambilan — di sinilah tenaga kerja benar-benar dihabiskan.**

segments.src: Order picking is typically the single largest labor line in a distribution center, and in manual operations, studies consistently find that *walking* eats roughly half of a picker's time.
segments.tr: Pengambilan pesanan biasanya merupakan pos tenaga kerja terbesar di pusat distribusi, dan dalam operasi manual, studi secara konsisten menemukan bahwa *berjalan kaki* menghabiskan sekitar separuh waktu seorang picker.

segments.src: That's why almost every improvement idea is really a walking-reduction idea:
segments.tr: Itulah sebabnya hampir setiap gagasan perbaikan sebenarnya adalah gagasan untuk mengurangi jalan kaki:

segments.src: - **Slotting:** put the fast movers in the "golden zone" (waist-to-shoulder height, near the pack stations) and the slow movers up high or far back. Usually driven by **ABC analysis** — the top ~20% of SKUs often drive ~80% of the picks.
segments.tr: - **Slotting:** letakkan barang yang bergerak cepat di "zona emas" (setinggi pinggang hingga bahu, dekat stasiun pengemasan) dan barang yang bergerak lambat di tempat tinggi atau jauh di belakang. Biasanya didorong oleh **analisis ABC** — sekitar 20% SKU teratas sering menyumbang sekitar 80% dari pengambilan.

segments.src: - **Batch picking:** grab items for 12 orders in one trip instead of walking the aisle 12 times.
segments.tr: - **Batch picking:** ambil barang untuk 12 pesanan dalam satu perjalanan, alih-alih berjalan menyusuri lorong 12 kali.

segments.src: - **Zone picking:** each worker owns one area; totes move between zones by conveyor.
segments.tr: - **Zone picking:** setiap pekerja bertanggung jawab atas satu area; keranjang berpindah antarzona melalui konveyor.

segments.src: - **Goods-to-person:** stop walking entirely — bring the shelf to the human.
segments.tr: - **Goods-to-person:** hentikan jalan kaki sepenuhnya — bawa rak ke manusia.

segments.src: Automation — how much steel do you buy?**
segments.tr: Otomatisasi — seberapa banyak baja yang ingin Anda beli?**

segments.src: The menu runs from cheap and flexible to expensive and fast: barcode scanners → pick-to-light and voice picking → conveyors and sorters → **AMRs** (mobile robots that carry totes or whole shelving pods) → **AS/RS** (automated storage and retrieval systems: cranes or shuttles in dense racking).
segments.tr: Menunya mulai dari yang murah dan fleksibel hingga yang mahal dan cepat: pemindai barcode → pick-to-light dan voice picking → konveyor dan sorter → **AMR** (robot seluler yang membawa keranjang atau seluruh modul rak) → **AS/RS** (sistem penyimpanan dan pengambilan otomatis: crane atau shuttle di rak padat).

segments.src: The trade-off is blunt:
segments.tr: Pertukarannya cukup jelas:

segments.src: fixed automation  = high throughput, low flexibility, long payback (often 5-10 years)
segments.tr: fixed automation  = high throughput, low flexibility, long payback (often 5-10 years)

segments.src: mobile robots     = lower throughput per unit, but you can add or remove them
segments.tr: mobile robots     = lower throughput per unit, but you can add or remove them

segments.src: Fixed conveyor is poured concrete — great if your volume and product mix are stable for a decade.
segments.tr: Konveyor tetap adalah beton cor — sangat baik jika volume dan campuran produk Anda stabil selama satu dekade.

segments.src: If your SKU mix changes every season, that steel becomes a cage.
segments.tr: Jika campuran SKU Anda berubah setiap musim, baja itu menjadi sangkar.

segments.src: And none of it works without a **WMS** (warehouse management system) telling everyone and everything where to go.
segments.tr: Dan semua itu tidak akan berjalan tanpa **WMS** (sistem manajemen gudang) yang memberi tahu semua orang dan semua hal ke mana harus pergi.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dalam Kehidupan Sehari-hari

segments.src: You order a phone case at 11 p.m.
segments.tr: Anda memesan casing ponsel pukul 23.00

segments.src: on a Tuesday and it's on your porch Thursday morning.
segments.tr: pada hari Selasa dan barang itu sudah ada di depan rumah Anda Kamis pagi.

segments.src: Here's what those four decisions did for you.
segments.tr: Inilah yang dilakukan keempat keputusan tersebut untuk Anda.

segments.src: **Siting:** the item shipped from a fulfillment center outside Columbus, Ohio — one of the most crowded distribution corridors in the country, along with Indianapolis, Memphis, and California's Inland Empire.
segments.tr: **Penempatan lokasi:** barang dikirim dari pusat fulfillment di luar Columbus, Ohio — salah satu koridor distribusi terpadat di negara ini, bersama Indianapolis, Memphis, dan Inland Empire di California.

segments.src: Central Ohio is popular partly because a single day's truck drive from there reaches a very large share of the U.S.
segments.tr: Ohio Tengah populer sebagian karena dalam satu hari perjalanan truk dari sana, sebagian sangat besar dari jumlah

segments.src: population.
segments.tr: penduduk Amerika Serikat dapat dijangkau.

segments.src: The company paid for that: industrial space is quoted in dollars per square foot per year, and rents run from the high single digits in parts of the Midwest to well into the teens and above in Southern California.
segments.tr: Perusahaan membayar untuk itu: ruang industri dihargai dalam dolar per kaki persegi per tahun, dan sewa berkisar dari satu digit tinggi di beberapa wilayah Midwest hingga belasan dolar atau lebih di California Selatan.

segments.src: That premium buys a delivery promise.
segments.tr: Premi itu membeli janji pengiriman.

segments.src: **Layout and slotting:** your case wasn't stored next to other phone cases.
segments.tr: **Tata letak dan slotting:** casing Anda tidak disimpan di samping casing ponsel lain.

segments.src: Many large fulfillment centers use *random* (sometimes called chaotic) storage — items go wherever there's an open bin, and the WMS remembers.
segments.tr: Banyak pusat fulfillment besar menggunakan penyimpanan *acak* (kadang disebut kacau) — barang ditempatkan di bin yang kosong, dan WMS yang mengingatnya.

segments.src: It sounds like chaos; it's actually better cube utilization and shorter walks, because popular items end up scattered near many pick paths instead of clustered in one aisle everyone has to visit.
segments.tr: Kedengarannya kacau; sebenarnya ini justru pemanfaatan ruang yang lebih baik dan jalan kaki yang lebih pendek, karena barang populer tersebar di dekat banyak jalur pengambilan, alih-alih menumpuk di satu lorong yang harus dikunjungi semua orang.

segments.src: **Picking:** a worker pushing a cart of totes picked your case as part of a batch of 20-some orders, guided by a handheld that sequenced the route.
segments.tr: **Pengambilan:** seorang pekerja yang mendorong troli berisi keranjang mengambil casing Anda sebagai bagian dari batch lebih dari 20 pesanan, dipandu oleh perangkat genggam yang mengurutkan rute.

segments.src: Or a robot drove a whole shelving pod to a stationary picker who never took a step.
segments.tr: Atau sebuah robot membawa seluruh modul rak ke picker yang diam dan tidak pernah melangkah.

segments.src: **Automation:** at pack-out, your box hit a conveyor, got weighed (a weight mismatch flags a wrong-item pick), passed a scanner, and a sorter diverted it down the chute for the right carrier trailer.
segments.tr: **Otomatisasi:** di tahap pengemasan, kardus Anda masuk ke konveyor, ditimbang (ketidaksesuaian berat menandai salah ambil barang), melewati pemindai, dan sorter mengalihkannya ke saluran untuk trailer kurir yang tepat.

segments.src: That trailer left on a scheduled cutoff — miss the cutoff and "Thursday" becomes "Friday."
segments.tr: Trailer itu berangkat sesuai batas waktu yang dijadwalkan — jika terlewat batas waktu, "Kamis" menjadi "Jumat".

segments.src: Which is the real lesson: the delivery date you saw at checkout was mostly decided by a building's floor plan and a truck's departure time.
segments.tr: Itulah pelajaran sebenarnya: tanggal pengiriman yang Anda lihat saat checkout sebagian besar ditentukan oleh denah sebuah gedung dan waktu keberangkatan sebuah truk.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Ringkasan Tiga Baris

segments.src: 1. Warehouse siting trades outbound speed and cost against land, labor, and inbound freight — you can't optimize all of them.
segments.tr: 1. Penempatan gudang menukar kecepatan dan biaya pengiriman keluar dengan tanah, tenaga kerja, dan biaya pengiriman masuk — Anda tidak bisa mengoptimalkan semuanya sekaligus.

segments.src: 2. Layout and slotting exist to kill walking, because walking is roughly half of picking time and picking is the biggest labor cost.
segments.tr: 2. Tata letak dan slotting ada untuk menghilangkan jalan kaki, karena berjalan kaki sekitar separuh dari waktu pengambilan dan pengambilan adalah biaya tenaga kerja terbesar.

segments.src: 3. Automation buys throughput with capital and gives up flexibility — the right level depends on how stable your volume and product mix are.
segments.tr: 3. Otomatisasi membeli throughput dengan modal dan mengorbankan fleksibilitas — tingkat yang tepat bergantung pada seberapa stabil volume dan campuran produk Anda.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Kuis Mandiri

segments.src: **1.** In a typical manual, picker-to-goods operation, the largest single chunk of a picker's time goes to:
segments.tr: **1.** Dalam operasi manual tipe picker-ke-barang, bagian terbesar waktu picker dihabiskan untuk:

segments.src: A) scanning barcodes
segments.tr: A) memindai barcode

segments.src: B) traveling (walking) between locations
segments.tr: B) berjalan (berpindah) antarlokasi

segments.src: C) packing cartons
segments.tr: C) mengemas kardus

segments.src: D) waiting for a forklift
segments.tr: D) menunggu forklift

segments.src: **2.** (O/X) Placing your fastest-moving SKUs at waist height near the pack stations is called *slotting*, and its main purpose is to reduce travel time.
segments.tr: **2.** (O/X) Menempatkan SKU yang paling cepat bergerak di ketinggian pinggang dekat stasiun pengemasan disebut *slotting*, dan tujuan utamanya adalah mengurangi waktu tempuh.

segments.src: **3.** A retailer's volume triples every Q4 and its product mix changes every season.
segments.tr: **3.** Volume sebuah peritel meningkat tiga kali lipat setiap Q4 dan campuran produknya berubah setiap musim.

segments.src: Which automation choice generally fits better?
segments.tr: Pilihan otomatisasi mana yang umumnya lebih cocok?

segments.src: A) A fixed conveyor-and-sortation system sized for peak
segments.tr: A) Sistem konveyor dan sortasi tetap yang dirancang untuk puncak

segments.src: B) Mobile robots (AMRs) that can be added or removed as volume changes
segments.tr: B) Robot seluler (AMR) yang dapat ditambah atau dikurangi seiring perubahan volume

segments.src: C) A full AS/RS crane system
segments.tr: C) Sistem crane AS/RS penuh

segments.src: D) No technology at all
segments.tr: D) Tanpa teknologi sama sekali

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Istilah Hari Ini

segments.src: - **Slotting** — deciding which item goes in which storage location, usually to minimize picker travel.
segments.tr: - **Slotting** — menentukan item mana yang masuk ke lokasi penyimpanan mana, biasanya untuk meminimalkan jarak tempuh picker.

segments.src: - **ABC analysis** — ranking SKUs by activity (A = fastest moving) so storage and effort go where the volume is.
segments.tr: - **Analisis ABC** — memeringkat SKU berdasarkan aktivitas (A = paling cepat bergerak) agar penyimpanan dan tenaga kerja difokuskan ke tempat volumenya berada.

segments.src: - **Batch picking** — picking items for multiple orders in a single trip through the warehouse, then sorting them by order afterward.
segments.tr: - **Batch picking** — mengambil barang untuk beberapa pesanan dalam satu perjalanan melalui gudang, lalu mengurutkannya per pesanan setelahnya.

segments.src: - **Goods-to-person (G2P)** — automation that brings inventory to a stationary worker instead of sending the worker to the inventory.
segments.tr: - **Goods-to-person (G2P)** — otomatisasi yang membawa persediaan ke pekerja yang diam, alih-alih mengirim pekerja ke persediaan.

segments.src: - **Cross-docking** — moving freight straight from an inbound trailer to an outbound one with little or no storage in between.
segments.tr: - **Cross-docking** — memindahkan barang langsung dari trailer masuk ke trailer keluar dengan sedikit atau tanpa penyimpanan di antaranya.

segments.src: *Answers: **1) B** — travel typically accounts for around half of order-picking time in manual operations, which is why layout and slotting matter so much.
segments.tr: *Jawaban: **1) B** — berjalan biasanya memakan sekitar separuh waktu pengambilan pesanan dalam operasi manual, itulah sebabnya tata letak dan slotting sangat penting.

segments.src: **2) O (True)** — slotting fast movers into the golden zone near pack-out shortens both walking and reaching.
segments.tr: **2) O (Benar)** — menempatkan barang yang bergerak cepat di zona emas dekat stasiun pengemasan memperpendek jalan kaki sekaligus jangkauan.

segments.src: **3) B** — AMRs scale incrementally and tolerate a changing SKU mix; fixed conveyor and AS/RS deliver higher throughput but lock in a layout and need stable, predictable volume to justify the payback period.*
segments.tr: **3) B** — AMR dapat diskalakan secara bertahap dan menyesuaikan dengan campuran SKU yang berubah; konveyor tetap dan AS/RS memberikan throughput lebih tinggi tetapi mengunci tata letak dan membutuhkan volume yang stabil dan dapat diprediksi untuk membenarkan periode pengembalian investasi.*

segments.src: The menu runs from cheap and flexible to expensive and fast: barcode scanners → pick-to-light and voice picking → conveyors and sorters → **AMRs** (mobile robots that carry totes or whole shelving pods) → **AS/RS** (automated storage and retrieval systems: cranes or shuttles in dense racking).
segments.tr: 選択肢は、安価で柔軟なものから高価で高速なものまであります：バーコードスキャナー → ピックトゥライトや音声ピッキング → コンベアやソーター → **AMR**（トートや棚ごと運ぶ自律走行搬送ロボット） → **AS/RS**（高密度ラックでクレーンやシャトルを使う自動倉庫システム）。

segments.src: The trade-off is blunt:
segments.tr: トレードオフは率直に言えば次のとおりです：

segments.src: fixed automation  = high throughput, low flexibility, long payback (often 5-10 years)
segments.tr: fixed automation  = high throughput, low flexibility, long payback (often 5-10 years)

segments.src: mobile robots     = lower throughput per unit, but you can add or remove them

segments.src: Fixed conveyor is poured concrete — great if your volume and product mix are stable for a decade.

segments.src: If your SKU mix changes every season, that steel becomes a cage.
segments.tr: SKU構成が季節ごとに変わるなら、その鋼材は檻になります。

segments.src: And none of it works without a **WMS** (warehouse management system) telling everyone and everything where to go.
segments.tr: そして、どれも**WMS**（倉庫管理システム）が全員と全機器に行き先を指示しなければ機能しません。

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap

segments.src: 1. Warehouse siting trades outbound speed and cost against land, labor, and inbound freight — you can't optimize all of them.

segments.src: 3. Automation buys throughput with capital and gives up flexibility — the right level depends on how stable your volume and product mix are.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日の用語

segments.src: - **Slotting** — deciding which item goes in which storage location, usually to minimize picker travel.
segments.tr: - **スロッティング** ― どの商品をどの保管場所に置くかを決めること。通常はピッカーの移動距離を最小化するため。

segments.src: - **ABC analysis** — ranking SKUs by activity (A = fastest moving) so storage and effort go where the volume is.
segments.tr: - **ABC分析** ― SKUを動きの量でランク付けすること（A = 最も速く動く）。保管と作業を出荷量の多いところに集中させるため。

segments.src: - **Batch picking** — picking items for multiple orders in a single trip through the warehouse, then sorting them by order afterward.
segments.tr: - **バッチピッキング** ― 倉庫内の1回の移動で複数の注文の商品をピッキングし、その後注文ごとに仕分けること。

segments.src: - **Goods-to-person (G2P)** — automation that brings inventory to a stationary worker instead of sending the worker to the inventory.
segments.tr: - **グッズ・ツー・パーソン（G2P）** ― 作業者を在庫の所へ送るのではなく、在庫を静止した作業者のところへ運ぶ自動化。

segments.src: - **Cross-docking** — moving freight straight from an inbound trailer to an outbound one with little or no storage in between.
segments.tr: - **クロスドッキング** ― 保管をほとんど、またはまったく挟まず、入荷トレーラーから出荷トレーラーへ貨物を直接移すこと。

segments.src: *Answers: **1) B** — travel typically accounts for around half of order-picking time in manual operations, which is why layout and slotting matter so much.
segments.tr: *解答：**1) B** ― 手作業のオーダーピッキングでは移動が通常ピッキング時間のおよそ半分を占めるため、レイアウトとスロッティングが非常に重要です。

segments.src: **2) O (True)** — slotting fast movers into the golden zone near pack-out shortens both walking and reaching.
segments.tr: **2) O（正しい）** ― 梱包ステーション近くのゴールデンゾーンに動きの速い商品をスロッティングすると、歩行と手を伸ばす動作の両方が短くなります。

segments.src: **3) B** — AMRs scale incrementally and tolerate a changing SKU mix; fixed conveyor and AS/RS deliver higher throughput but lock in a layout and need stable, predictable volume to justify the payback period.*
segments.tr: **3) B** ― AMRは段階的に拡張でき、変化するSKU構成にも対応できます。固定式コンベアとAS/RSは高いスループットをもたらしますが、レイアウトを固定し、投資回収期間を正当化するには安定した予測可能な出荷量が必要です。*

de.title: [Logistik 101 #7] Das Gebäude, das entscheidet, ob Ihre Bestellung morgen ankommt

segments.src: > A warehouse isn't a place to park boxes — it's a machine for turning space, walking distance, and labor into delivery speed.
segments.tr: > Ein Lager ist kein Ort zum Abstellen von Kartons – es ist eine Maschine, die Fläche, Laufwege und Arbeitskraft in Liefergeschwindigkeit verwandelt.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Das heutige Konzept

segments.src: Say "warehouse" and most people picture shelves.
segments.tr: Wenn man "Lager" hört, denken die meisten an Regale.

segments.src: In supply chain terms, though, a warehouse is a decision stack: four choices that together determine how fast and how cheaply an order gets out the door.
segments.tr: In der Lieferkette ist ein Lager jedoch ein Entscheidungsstapel: vier Entscheidungen, die zusammen bestimmen, wie schnell und wie günstig eine Bestellung das Haus verlässt.

segments.src: Siting — where do you put the building?**
segments.tr: Standort – wo stellt man das Gebäude hin?**

segments.src: Every location is a tug-of-war.
segments.tr: Jeder Standort ist ein Tauziehen.

segments.src: Sit close to your customers and outbound delivery gets cheap and fast, but land and labor cost more.
segments.tr: Liegt man nah bei den Kunden, wird die Auslieferung günstig und schnell, aber Grundstück und Personal kosten mehr.

segments.src: Sit close to the port or the factory and inbound freight gets cheap, but every order travels farther.
segments.tr: Liegt man nah am Hafen oder am Werk, wird der Wareneingang günstig, aber jede Bestellung legt einen längeren Weg zurück.

segments.src: Planners also weigh labor availability (can you actually hire 400 people in November?), highway and rail access, property taxes, and how many other companies are already bidding for the same workers.
segments.tr: Planer wägen außerdem die Verfügbarkeit von Arbeitskräften ab (kann man im November tatsächlich 400 Leute einstellen?), den Anschluss an Autobahn und Schiene, die Grundsteuer und wie viele andere Unternehmen bereits um dieselben Arbeitskräfte konkurrieren.

segments.src: A common starting tool is the **center of gravity method**: plot demand on a map, weight each point by volume, and find the balance point.
segments.tr: Ein gängiges Einstiegswerkzeug ist die **Schwerpunktmethode**: Man trägt die Nachfrage auf einer Karte ein, gewichtet jeden Punkt nach Volumen und sucht den Gleichgewichtspunkt.

segments.src: It's a first draft, not an answer — the real site has to have power, a highway ramp, and people.
segments.tr: Das ist ein erster Entwurf, keine Antwort – der tatsächliche Standort braucht Strom, eine Autobahnauffahrt und Personal.

segments.src: Layout — how does product flow through it?**
segments.tr: Layout – wie fließen die Waren hindurch?**

segments.src: Goods generally move: receiving → putaway → storage → picking → packing → shipping.
segments.tr: Waren bewegen sich in der Regel so: Wareneingang → Einlagerung → Lagerung → Kommissionierung → Verpackung → Versand.

segments.src: The layout's job is to make that path short and keep flows from crossing.
segments.tr: Die Aufgabe des Layouts ist es, diesen Weg kurz zu halten und Warenströme nicht kreuzen zu lassen.

segments.src: Two classic shapes:
segments.tr: Zwei klassische Formen:

segments.src: - **I-flow (through-flow):** docks on opposite ends, product moves straight across. Simple, good for high-volume, cross-dock-heavy operations.
segments.tr: - **I-Fluss (Durchlauf):** Rampen an gegenüberliegenden Enden, die Ware wandert geradlinig hindurch. Einfach, gut für Betriebe mit hohem Volumen und viel Cross-Docking.

segments.src: - **U-flow:** receiving and shipping on the same wall. Fast-moving items sit near that wall so they're close to both, and one dock crew can flex between inbound and outbound.
segments.tr: - **U-Fluss:** Wareneingang und Versand an derselben Wand. Schnelldreher liegen nah an dieser Wand und damit nahe an beiden Vorgängen, und ein Rampenteam kann flexibel zwischen Eingang und Ausgang wechseln.

segments.src: Picking — where the labor actually goes.**
segments.tr: Kommissionierung – wo die Arbeitskraft tatsächlich hingeht.**

segments.src: Order picking is typically the single largest labor line in a distribution center, and in manual operations, studies consistently find that *walking* eats roughly half of a picker's time.
segments.tr: Die Auftragskommissionierung ist in einem Distributionszentrum typischerweise der größte einzelne Personalposten, und in manuellen Betrieben zeigen Studien übereinstimmend, dass das *Gehen* etwa die Hälfte der Zeit eines Kommissionierers frisst.

segments.src: That's why almost every improvement idea is really a walking-reduction idea:
segments.tr: Deshalb ist fast jede Verbesserungsidee eigentlich eine Idee zur Reduzierung der Wegstrecke:

segments.src: - **Slotting:** put the fast movers in the "golden zone" (waist-to-shoulder height, near the pack stations) and the slow movers up high or far back. Usually driven by **ABC analysis** — the top ~20% of SKUs often drive ~80% of the picks.
segments.tr: - **Slotting:** Schnelldreher in die "goldene Zone" (Hüfte bis Schulter, nahe den Packplätzen) legen und Langsamdreher nach oben oder weit nach hinten. Meist gesteuert durch eine **ABC-Analyse** – die oberen ~20 % der Artikel verursachen oft ~80 % der Entnahmen.

segments.src: - **Batch picking:** grab items for 12 orders in one trip instead of walking the aisle 12 times.
segments.tr: - **Batch-Kommissionierung:** Artikel für 12 Aufträge auf einer Runde einsammeln, statt zwölfmal durch den Gang zu laufen.

segments.src: - **Zone picking:** each worker owns one area; totes move between zones by conveyor.
segments.tr: - **Zonenkommissionierung:** Jeder Mitarbeiter ist für einen Bereich zuständig; Behälter wandern per Förderband zwischen den Zonen.

segments.src: - **Goods-to-person:** stop walking entirely — bring the shelf to the human.
segments.tr: - **Goods-to-Person:** Gar nicht mehr gehen – das Regal kommt zum Menschen.

segments.tr: ## Zusammenfassung in drei Zeilen

segments.src: 1. Warehouse siting trades outbound speed and cost against land, labor, and inbound freight — you can't optimize all of them.
segments.tr: 1. Der Lagerstandort tauscht Ausgangsgeschwindigkeit und Kosten gegen Grundstück, Personal und Wareneingangsfracht – alle lassen sich nicht gleichzeitig optimieren.

segments.src: 2. Layout and slotting exist to kill walking, because walking is roughly half of picking time and picking is the biggest labor cost.
segments.tr: 2. Layout und Slotting dienen dazu, Wegstrecken zu vermeiden, denn Gehen ist etwa die Hälfte der Kommissionierzeit und die Kommissionierung der größte Personalposten.

segments.src: 3. Automation buys throughput with capital and gives up flexibility — the right level depends on how stable your volume and product mix are.
segments.tr: 3. Automatisierung erkauft Durchsatz mit Kapital und gibt Flexibilität auf – das richtige Maß hängt davon ab, wie stabil Volumen und Sortimentsmix sind.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Selbsttest

segments.src: **1.** In a typical manual, picker-to-goods operation, the largest single chunk of a picker's time goes to:
segments.tr: **1.** Bei einer typischen manuellen Kommissionierung Mensch-zur-Ware: Der größte Einzelanteil der Zeit eines Kommissionierers entfällt auf:

segments.src: A) scanning barcodes
segments.tr: A) Scannen von Barcodes

segments.src: B) traveling (walking) between locations
segments.tr: B) Gehen (Laufen) zwischen den Lagerplätzen

segments.src: C) packing cartons
segments.tr: C) Packen von Kartons

segments.src: D) waiting for a forklift
segments.tr: D) Warten auf einen Gabelstapler

segments.src: **2.** (O/X) Placing your fastest-moving SKUs at waist height near the pack stations is called *slotting*, and its main purpose is to reduce travel time.
segments.tr: **2.** (R/F) Schnelldreher auf Hüfthöhe nahe den Packplätzen zu legen heißt *Slotting*, und sein Hauptzweck ist die Verkürzung der Wegzeit.

segments.src: **3.** A retailer's volume triples every Q4 and its product mix changes every season.
segments.tr: Das Volumen eines Händlers verdreifacht sich jedes Q4, und der Produktmix ändert sich jede Saison.

segments.src: Which automation choice generally fits better?
segments.tr: Welche Automatisierungsoption passt in der Regel besser?

segments.src: A) A fixed conveyor-and-sortation system sized for peak
segments.tr: A) Eine feste Förderband- und Sortieranlage, auf Spitzenlast dimensioniert

segments.src: B) Mobile robots (AMRs) that can be added or removed as volume changes
segments.tr: B) Mobile Roboter (AMRs), die je nach Volumen hinzugefügt oder entfernt werden können

segments.src: C) A full AS/RS crane system
segments.tr: C) Ein komplettes AS/RS-Kransystem

segments.src: D) No technology at all
segments.tr: D) Gar keine Technik

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Begriffe des Tages

segments.src: - **Slotting** — deciding which item goes in which storage location, usually to minimize picker travel.
segments.tr: - **Slotting** — Festlegen, welcher Artikel an welchem Lagerplatz liegt, meist um den Laufweg der Kommissionierer zu minimieren.

segments.src: - **ABC analysis** — ranking SKUs by activity (A = fastest moving) so storage and effort go where the volume is.
segments.tr: - **ABC-Analyse** — Einordnung der Artikel nach Umschlag (A = schnellster Umschlag), damit Lagerplatz und Aufwand dort eingesetzt werden, wo das Volumen liegt.

segments.src: - **Batch picking** — picking items for multiple orders in a single trip through the warehouse, then sorting them by order afterward.
segments.tr: - **Batch-Kommissionierung** — Kommissionieren der Artikel mehrerer Aufträge in einem einzigen Rundgang durch das Lager und anschließendes Sortieren nach Auftrag.

segments.src: - **Goods-to-person (G2P)** — automation that brings inventory to a stationary worker instead of sending the worker to the inventory.
segments.tr: - **Goods-to-Person (G2P)** — Automatisierung, die den Bestand zu einem stationären Mitarbeiter bringt, statt den Mitarbeiter zum Bestand zu schicken.

segments.src: - **Cross-docking** — moving freight straight from an inbound trailer to an outbound one with little or no storage in between.
segments.tr: - **Cross-Docking** — Fracht direkt von einem Eingangs-Lkw auf einen Ausgangs-Lkw umladen, mit wenig oder gar keiner Zwischenlagerung.

segments.src: *Answers: **1) B** — travel typically accounts for around half of order-picking time in manual operations, which is why layout and slotting matter so much.
segments.tr: *Lösungen: **1) B** — Das Gehen macht bei manueller Kommissionierung typischerweise etwa die Hälfte der Kommissionierzeit aus, weshalb Layout und Slotting so wichtig sind.

segments.src: **2) O (True)** — slotting fast movers into the golden zone near pack-out shortens both walking and reaching.
segments.tr: **2) R (Richtig)** — Schnelldreher in der goldenen Zone nahe dem Packplatz verkürzen sowohl das Gehen als auch das Greifen.

segments.src: **3) B** — AMRs scale incrementally and tolerate a changing SKU mix; fixed conveyor and AS/RS deliver higher throughput but lock in a layout and need stable, predictable volume to justify the payback period.*
segments.tr: **3) B** — AMRs skalieren schrittweise und vertragen einen wechselnden Sortimentsmix; feste Förderbänder und AS/RS liefern mehr Durchsatz, legen aber ein Layout fest und benötigen stabiles, planbares Volumen, um die Amortisationszeit zu rechtfertigen.*

vi.title: [Logistics 101 #7] Tòa nhà quyết định đơn hàng của bạn có đến nơi vào ngày mai hay không

segments.src: > A warehouse isn't a place to park boxes — it's a machine for turning space, walking distance, and labor into delivery speed.
segments.tr: > Kho hàng không phải là nơi để chất hàng — mà là một cỗ máy biến không gian, khoảng cách đi bộ và sức lao động thành tốc độ giao hàng.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Khái niệm hôm nay

segments.src: Say "warehouse" and most people picture shelves.
segments.tr: Nhắc đến “kho hàng”, hầu hết mọi người nghĩ ngay đến những kệ hàng.

segments.src: In supply chain terms, though, a warehouse is a decision stack: four choices that together determine how fast and how cheaply an order gets out the door.
segments.tr: Tuy nhiên, theo thuật ngữ chuỗi cung ứng, kho hàng là một chuỗi quyết định: bốn lựa chọn cùng nhau quyết định đơn hàng được xuất đi nhanh và rẻ đến mức nào.

segments.src: Siting — where do you put the building?**
segments.tr: Chọn vị trí — đặt tòa nhà ở đâu?**

segments.src: Every location is a tug-of-war.
segments.tr: Mỗi vị trí đều là một cuộc kéo co.

segments.src: Sit close to your customers and outbound delivery gets cheap and fast, but land and labor cost more.
segments.tr: Đặt gần khách hàng thì giao hàng đi ra nhanh và rẻ, nhưng giá đất và nhân công cao hơn.

segments.src: Sit close to the port or the factory and inbound freight gets cheap, but every order travels farther.
segments.tr: Đặt gần cảng hoặc nhà máy thì vận chuyển hàng nhập rẻ, nhưng mỗi đơn hàng phải đi xa hơn.

segments.src: Planners also weigh labor availability (can you actually hire 400 people in November?), highway and rail access, property taxes, and how many other companies are already bidding for the same workers.
segments.tr: Người lập kế hoạch cũng cân nhắc nguồn lao động (liệu có thể tuyển 400 người vào tháng 11 không?), khả năng tiếp cận đường cao tốc và đường sắt, thuế bất động sản, và có bao nhiêu công ty khác đang cạnh tranh để thuê cùng lực lượng lao động đó.

segments.src: A common starting tool is the **center of gravity method**: plot demand on a map, weight each point by volume, and find the balance point.
segments.tr: Một công cụ khởi đầu phổ biến là **phương pháp trọng tâm**: đánh dấu nhu cầu trên bản đồ, gán trọng số cho từng điểm theo khối lượng, rồi tìm điểm cân bằng.

segments.src: It's a first draft, not an answer — the real site has to have power, a highway ramp, and people.
segments.tr: Đây chỉ là bản nháp đầu tiên, không phải đáp án — địa điểm thực tế phải có điện, lối lên đường cao tốc và nhân lực.

segments.src: Layout — how does product flow through it?**
segments.tr: Bố trí mặt bằng — hàng hóa di chuyển qua kho như thế nào?**

segments.src: Goods generally move: receiving → putaway → storage → picking → packing → shipping.
segments.tr: Hàng hóa thường di chuyển theo trình tự: tiếp nhận → cất vào vị trí → lưu trữ → lấy hàng → đóng gói → xuất hàng.

segments.src: The layout's job is to make that path short and keep flows from crossing.
segments.tr: Nhiệm vụ của bố trí mặt bằng là làm cho lộ trình đó ngắn và không để các luồng hàng giao nhau.

segments.src: Two classic shapes:
segments.tr: Hai dạng bố trí kinh điển:

segments.src: - **I-flow (through-flow):** docks on opposite ends, product moves straight across. Simple, good for high-volume, cross-dock-heavy operations.
segments.tr: - **Luồng chữ I (xuyên suốt):** cửa bốc dỡ ở hai đầu đối diện, hàng đi thẳng qua. Đơn giản, phù hợp với hoạt động khối lượng lớn và nhiều cross-dock.

segments.src: - **U-flow:** receiving and shipping on the same wall. Fast-moving items sit near that wall so they're close to both, and one dock crew can flex between inbound and outbound.
segments.tr: - **Luồng chữ U:** tiếp nhận và xuất hàng nằm cùng một bức tường. Các mặt hàng bán chạy đặt gần bức tường đó để gần cả hai đầu, và một đội bốc dỡ có thể linh hoạt chuyển giữa nhập và xuất.

segments.src: Picking — where the labor actually goes.**
segments.tr: Lấy hàng — nơi sức lao động thực sự được sử dụng.**

segments.src: Order picking is typically the single largest labor line in a distribution center, and in manual operations, studies consistently find that *walking* eats roughly half of a picker's time.
segments.tr: Lấy hàng theo đơn thường là hạng mục nhân công lớn nhất trong trung tâm phân phối, và trong các hoạt động thủ công, các nghiên cứu luôn cho thấy *đi bộ* chiếm khoảng một nửa thời gian của người lấy hàng.

segments.src: That's why almost every improvement idea is really a walking-reduction idea:
segments.tr: Đó là lý do hầu hết mọi ý tưởng cải tiến thực chất là ý tưởng giảm quãng đường đi bộ:

segments.src: - **Slotting:** put the fast movers in the "golden zone" (waist-to-shoulder height, near the pack stations) and the slow movers up high or far back. Usually driven by **ABC analysis** — the top ~20% of SKUs often drive ~80% of the picks.
segments.tr: - **Sắp xếp vị trí (slotting):** đặt các mặt hàng bán nhanh vào “vùng vàng” (ngang thắt lưng đến vai, gần trạm đóng gói) và các mặt hàng bán chậm lên cao hoặc xa phía trong. Thường dựa trên **phân tích ABC** — khoảng 20% SKU hàng đầu thường chiếm khoảng 80% số lần lấy hàng.

segments.src: - **Batch picking:** grab items for 12 orders in one trip instead of walking the aisle 12 times.
segments.tr: - **Lấy hàng theo lô (batch picking):** lấy hàng cho 12 đơn trong một chuyến thay vì đi qua lối đi 12 lần.

segments.src: - **Zone picking:** each worker owns one area; totes move between zones by conveyor.
segments.tr: - **Lấy hàng theo khu (zone picking):** mỗi người phụ trách một khu vực; các thùng chứa được băng tải chuyển giữa các khu.

segments.src: - **Goods-to-person:** stop walking entirely — bring the shelf to the human.
segments.tr: - **Hàng đến người (goods-to-person):** không còn phải đi bộ — đưa kệ hàng đến người lao động.

segments.src: Automation — how much steel do you buy?**
segments.tr: Tự động hóa — nên mua bao nhiêu thiết bị?**

segments.src: The menu runs from cheap and flexible to expensive and fast: barcode scanners → pick-to-light and voice picking → conveyors and sorters → **AMRs** (mobile robots that carry totes or whole shelving pods) → **AS/RS** (automated storage and retrieval systems: cranes or shuttles in dense racking).
segments.tr: Các lựa chọn trải từ rẻ và linh hoạt đến đắt và nhanh: máy quét mã vạch → chỉ dẫn lấy hàng bằng đèn hoặc giọng nói → băng tải và máy phân loại → **AMR** (robot di động chở thùng chứa hoặc cả giá kệ) → **AS/RS** (hệ thống lưu trữ và truy xuất tự động: cần trục hoặc xe shuttle trong giá kệ dày đặc).

segments.src: The trade-off is blunt:
segments.tr: Sự đánh đổi rất rõ ràng:

segments.src: fixed automation  = high throughput, low flexibility, long payback (often 5-10 years)
segments.tr: fixed automation  = high throughput, low flexibility, long payback (often 5-10 years)

segments.src: mobile robots     = lower throughput per unit, but you can add or remove them
segments.tr: mobile robots     = lower throughput per unit, but you can add or remove them

segments.src: Fixed conveyor is poured concrete — great if your volume and product mix are stable for a decade.
segments.tr: Băng tải cố định giống như bê tông đổ sẵn — rất tốt nếu khối lượng và cơ cấu sản phẩm ổn định trong nhiều năm.

segments.src: If your SKU mix changes every season, that steel becomes a cage.
segments.tr: Nếu cơ cấu SKU thay đổi theo từng mùa, khối thép đó sẽ trở thành một cái lồng.

segments.src: And none of it works without a **WMS** (warehouse management system) telling everyone and everything where to go.
segments.tr: Và tất cả đều vô nghĩa nếu không có **WMS** (hệ thống quản lý kho) chỉ cho mọi người và mọi thứ biết phải đi đâu.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Trong đời sống hằng ngày

segments.src: You order a phone case at 11 p.m.
segments.tr: Bạn đặt một ốp điện thoại lúc 11 giờ đêm

segments.src: on a Tuesday and it's on your porch Thursday morning.
segments.tr: vào thứ Ba và sáng thứ Năm nó đã nằm trước hiên nhà.

segments.src: Here's what those four decisions did for you.
segments.tr: Bốn quyết định trên đã làm gì cho bạn?

segments.src: **Siting:** the item shipped from a fulfillment center outside Columbus, Ohio — one of the most crowded distribution corridors in the country, along with Indianapolis, Memphis, and California's Inland Empire.
segments.tr: **Vị trí:** món hàng được xuất từ một trung tâm thực hiện đơn hàng ở ngoại ô Columbus, Ohio — một trong những hành lang phân phối đông đúc nhất nước Mỹ, cùng với Indianapolis, Memphis và Inland Empire của California.

segments.src: Central Ohio is popular partly because a single day's truck drive from there reaches a very large share of the U.S.
segments.tr: Trung tâm Ohio được ưa chuộng một phần vì chỉ một ngày lái xe tải từ đây là có thể tới một tỷ lệ rất lớn

segments.src: population.
segments.tr: dân số Hoa Kỳ.

segments.src: The company paid for that: industrial space is quoted in dollars per square foot per year, and rents run from the high single digits in parts of the Midwest to well into the teens and above in Southern California.
segments.tr: Công ty đã trả khoản đó: mặt bằng công nghiệp được báo giá theo đô la mỗi foot vuông mỗi năm, và giá thuê dao động từ khoảng một chục đô la thấp ở một số vùng Trung Tây đến trên mười lăm đô la ở Nam California.

segments.src: That premium buys a delivery promise.
segments.tr: Khoản phí cao hơn đó mua được một lời hứa giao hàng.

segments.src: **Layout and slotting:** your case wasn't stored next to other phone cases.
segments.tr: **Bố trí và sắp xếp vị trí:** hộp của bạn không được cất cạnh các ốp điện thoại khác.

segments.src: Many large fulfillment centers use *random* (sometimes called chaotic) storage — items go wherever there's an open bin, and the WMS remembers.
segments.tr: Nhiều trung tâm thực hiện đơn hàng lớn sử dụng lưu trữ *ngẫu nhiên* (đôi khi gọi là hỗn loạn) — hàng hóa được đặt vào bất kỳ ô trống nào, và WMS ghi nhớ vị trí.

segments.src: It sounds like chaos; it's actually better cube utilization and shorter walks, because popular items end up scattered near many pick paths instead of clustered in one aisle everyone has to visit.
segments.tr: Nghe có vẻ hỗn loạn; thực ra lại tận dụng không gian tốt hơn và đường đi ngắn hơn, vì các mặt hàng phổ biến được rải rác gần nhiều lộ trình lấy hàng thay vì tập trung trong một lối đi mà ai cũng phải qua.

segments.src: **Picking:** a worker pushing a cart of totes picked your case as part of a batch of 20-some orders, guided by a handheld that sequenced the route.
segments.tr: **Lấy hàng:** một nhân viên đẩy xe chở các thùng chứa đã lấy hộp của bạn trong một lô gồm hơn 20 đơn, được dẫn đường bởi một thiết bị cầm tay sắp xếp lộ trình.

segments.src: Or a robot drove a whole shelving pod to a stationary picker who never took a step.
segments.tr: Hoặc một robot đã chở cả một giá kệ đến cho một nhân viên đứng yên, người không phải bước một bước nào.

segments.src: **Automation:** at pack-out, your box hit a conveyor, got weighed (a weight mismatch flags a wrong-item pick), passed a scanner, and a sorter diverted it down the chute for the right carrier trailer.
segments.tr: **Tự động hóa:** tại khâu đóng gói, hộp của bạn đi qua băng tải, được cân (chênh lệch khối lượng sẽ báo lỗi lấy sai hàng), qua máy quét, rồi máy phân loại chuyển nó xuống máng đúng cho xe tải của đơn vị vận chuyển.

segments.src: That trailer left on a scheduled cutoff — miss the cutoff and "Thursday" becomes "Friday."
segments.tr: Chiếc xe đó rời đi theo giờ cắt hàng đã định — trễ giờ cắt thì “thứ Năm” sẽ thành “thứ Sáu.”

segments.src: Which is the real lesson: the delivery date you saw at checkout was mostly decided by a building's floor plan and a truck's departure time.
segments.tr: Đó mới là bài học thực sự: ngày giao hàng bạn thấy khi thanh toán phần lớn đã được quyết định bởi sơ đồ mặt bằng của một tòa nhà và giờ khởi hành của một chiếc xe tải.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Tóm tắt ba dòng

segments.src: 1. Warehouse siting trades outbound speed and cost against land, labor, and inbound freight — you can't optimize all of them.
segments.tr: 1. Việc chọn vị trí kho đánh đổi tốc độ và chi phí xuất hàng với giá đất, nhân công và chi phí vận chuyển hàng nhập — bạn không thể tối ưu tất cả cùng lúc.

segments.src: 2. Layout and slotting exist to kill walking, because walking is roughly half of picking time and picking is the biggest labor cost.
segments.tr: 2. Bố trí mặt bằng và sắp xếp vị trí tồn tại để loại bỏ việc đi bộ, vì đi bộ chiếm khoảng một nửa thời gian lấy hàng và lấy hàng là chi phí nhân công lớn nhất.

segments.src: 3. Automation buys throughput with capital and gives up flexibility — the right level depends on how stable your volume and product mix are.
segments.tr: 3. Tự động hóa mua thông lượng bằng vốn và đánh đổi sự linh hoạt — mức độ phù hợp phụ thuộc vào việc khối lượng và cơ cấu sản phẩm của bạn ổn định đến đâu.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Tự kiểm tra

segments.src: **1.** In a typical manual, picker-to-goods operation, the largest single chunk of a picker's time goes to:
segments.tr: **1.** Trong một hoạt động lấy hàng thủ công điển hình, phần thời gian lớn nhất của người lấy hàng dành cho:

segments.src: A) scanning barcodes
segments.tr: A) quét mã vạch

segments.src: B) traveling (walking) between locations
segments.tr: B) di chuyển (đi bộ) giữa các vị trí

segments.src: C) packing cartons
segments.tr: C) đóng thùng

segments.src: D) waiting for a forklift
segments.tr: D) chờ xe nâng

segments.src: **2.** (O/X) Placing your fastest-moving SKUs at waist height near the pack stations is called *slotting*, and its main purpose is to reduce travel time.
segments.tr: **2.** (O/X) Đặt các SKU bán nhanh nhất ngang thắt lưng gần trạm đóng gói được gọi là *sắp xếp vị trí (slotting)*, và mục đích chính là giảm thời gian di chuyển.

segments.src: **3.** A retailer's volume triples every Q4 and its product mix changes every season.
segments.tr: **3.** Khối lượng của một nhà bán lẻ tăng gấp ba mỗi quý 4 và cơ cấu sản phẩm thay đổi theo từng mùa.

segments.src: Which automation choice generally fits better?
segments.tr: Lựa chọn tự động hóa nào thường phù hợp hơn?

segments.src: A) A fixed conveyor-and-sortation system sized for peak
segments.tr: A) Hệ thống băng tải cố định và phân loại được thiết kế cho giờ cao điểm

segments.src: B) Mobile robots (AMRs) that can be added or removed as volume changes
segments.tr: B) Robot di động (AMR) có thể thêm hoặc bớt khi khối lượng thay đổi

segments.src: C) A full AS/RS crane system
segments.tr: C) Hệ thống cần trục AS/RS đầy đủ

segments.src: D) No technology at all
segments.tr: D) Không dùng công nghệ nào cả

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Thuật ngữ hôm nay

segments.src: - **Slotting** — deciding which item goes in which storage location, usually to minimize picker travel.
segments.tr: - **Sắp xếp vị trí (Slotting)** — quyết định mặt hàng nào đặt ở vị trí lưu trữ nào, thường nhằm giảm thiểu quãng đường di chuyển của người lấy hàng.

segments.src: - **ABC analysis** — ranking SKUs by activity (A = fastest moving) so storage and effort go where the volume is.
segments.tr: - **Phân tích ABC** — xếp hạng SKU theo mức độ hoạt động (A = bán nhanh nhất) để việc lưu trữ và công sức được đặt vào nơi có khối lượng.

segments.src: - **Batch picking** — picking items for multiple orders in a single trip through the warehouse, then sorting them by order afterward.
segments.tr: - **Lấy hàng theo lô (Batch picking)** — lấy hàng cho nhiều đơn trong một chuyến đi qua kho, sau đó phân loại theo đơn.

segments.src: - **Goods-to-person (G2P)** — automation that brings inventory to a stationary worker instead of sending the worker to the inventory.
segments.tr: - **Hàng đến người (Goods-to-person, G2P)** — tự động hóa đưa hàng tồn kho đến người lao động đứng yên thay vì đưa người lao động đến hàng tồn kho.

segments.src: - **Cross-docking** — moving freight straight from an inbound trailer to an outbound one with little or no storage in between.
segments.tr: - **Cross-docking** — chuyển hàng trực tiếp từ xe tải nhập sang xe tải xuất với ít hoặc không lưu kho ở giữa.

segments.src: *Answers: **1) B** — travel typically accounts for around half of order-picking time in manual operations, which is why layout and slotting matter so much.
segments.tr: *Đáp án: **1) B** — di chuyển thường chiếm khoảng một nửa thời gian lấy hàng theo đơn trong hoạt động thủ công, đó là lý do bố trí mặt bằng và sắp xếp vị trí quan trọng đến vậy.

segments.src: **2) O (True)** — slotting fast movers into the golden zone near pack-out shortens both walking and reaching.
segments.tr: **2) O (Đúng)** — sắp xếp các mặt hàng bán nhanh vào vùng vàng gần khu đóng gói giúp rút ngắn cả việc đi bộ lẫn việc với tới.

segments.src: **3) B** — AMRs scale incrementally and tolerate a changing SKU mix; fixed conveyor and AS/RS deliver higher throughput but lock in a layout and need stable, predictable volume to justify the payback period.*
segments.tr: **3) B** — AMR có thể mở rộng từng bước và chịu được cơ cấu SKU thay đổi; băng tải cố định và AS/RS mang lại thông lượng cao hơn nhưng khóa cứng bố trí và cần khối lượng ổn định, dự đoán được để bù đắp thời gian hoàn vốn.*
